title: macOS LaunchAgent runs Zerus at daemon priority; CPU load starves the GUI until the watchdog aborts it
description: hgs-tray 0.42.2 on macOS 27 froze completely under 10 niced busy loops while other apps stayed responsive; after 30 s MainThreadWatchdog aborted it (crash 2026-10-15 14:19:39, main thread incidentally inside ActivityBrowser::paintEvent). Root cause: tray/packaging/com.hgdev.hgs-tray.plist has no ProcessType, so launchd spawns it as 'spawn type = daemon (3)' and clamps every thread to priority 20, below default-priority load (31) even when that load is niced. A thread QoS request from inside the process stays clamped at 20. Measured with launchd probes under 12 nice-0 busy loops: 2 ms CPU chunk p99 134 ms (daemon) vs 6.6 ms (ProcessType=Interactive) vs 4.7 ms (Interactive + USER_INTERACTIVE main-thread QoS). Fix: ProcessType=Interactive in the plist template, USER_INTERACTIVE QoS for the macOS GUI thread, docs for existing Homebrew autostart installs.
notes:
Verified on the live tray: same binary with only ProcessType=Interactive in the installed plist survived 45 s of 10 x nice-19 busy loops and 30 s of 12 x nice-0 busy loops; main thread PRI 31, 8-40% CPU, no watchdog line, no crash report (before: PRI 20, ~1.5% CPU, abort at 30 s). Branch fix/ui-hang-under-load in <project checkout>
Installed on the owner's Mac via tray/install.sh from fix/ui-hang-under-load (7743b87 + uncommitted fix): spawn type interactive, GUI thread PRI 37, workers 31; survived 45 s 10 x nice-19 + 30 s 12 x nice-0 busy loops without abort. Tests: 63/63 GUI ctest, test_macos_setup/bundle/tray_update/mac_install, check-source.py. Not committed yet (awaiting owner).
close_reason: Fixed in 9a461e2: tray LaunchAgent ProcessType Interactive + macOS GUI thread USER_INTERACTIVE QoS; zerus-setup reload hint; docs. Verified live on the owner's Mac (spawn type interactive, GUI thread 37, survived 75 s of 10-12 busy loops without watchdog abort); retained unchanged in 7a6274b with fully green CI run 38740582425 (macOS desktop, Arch desktop, CLI macos-15 green). title: Retire the Qt GUI completely: everything through hgs and Zerus Next
description:
Owner goal, 2026-10-29: Qt Zerus is removed completely in the end. Everything the Qt GUI (tray/src) does today must be possible through the hgs CLI plus the Tauri client (Zerus Next), on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Principles:
- UI goes to Zerus Next. Background behaviour and state that must outlive a closed window goes to hgs (CLI or its services), not into the client alone. Examples: automatic approval delivery, recovery, presence, attention notifications, the swarm and organization worker, worktree maintenance, update checks, run tokens, local organization data.
- Qt-only local data (organization JSON with run_groups, settings, drafts, desktop-previous, usage caches) migrates once, read-only. After the retirement no feature depends on a Qt file or process.
- Packaging (install.sh, tray/install.sh, mac-install.sh, AUR, Homebrew, the winget zip, the Dev feed) ships Zerus Next and hgs without the Qt GUI. Compatibility of the hgs CLI, HGS_* variables, state/config paths and application identifiers stays.
- The Mac switch (zerus-5wmh.13) is the first platform step, not the end.

First step: a complete inventory of tray/src responsibilities, mapped to hgs, Zerus Next, an existing bead, or a gap.

title: Tauri client (macOS): menu-bar item, single instance, window activation and login through the tray LaunchAgent
description:
Qt is an LSUIElement menu-bar app (MacTrayMenu, QtTrayIcon, SingleInstance). The new client must do the same before the switch (zerus-5wmh.13).

**Menu-bar item:** the status item with Qt's icon states and menu entries. Clicking it shows or hides the window. There is no Dock icon while hidden, as in Qt.

**Single instance:** use the same per-user lock and the same socket path as Qt's SingleInstance::key, with a name ending in /hgs-tray. Accept Qt's `show` and `sessions` lines. A second start forwards activation and exits. tray/update-installed.py finds this socket and sends `sessions` after starting the new GUI.

**Window activation:** bring the window to the front on activation.

**Launch at login:** only through the tray LaunchAgent template, tray/packaging/com.hgdev.hgs-tray.plist, which mac-install.sh and zerus-setup install. Spec row 299 rules out tauri-plugin-autostart. Keep KeepAlive Crashed and ProcessType Interactive as in Qt. Only the new client starts at login.

title: Tauri client (macOS): attention notifications under the Zerus identity, as Qt posts them
description:
The new client must post attention notifications on macOS, as Qt does today in tray/src/MacAttentionNotifier.mm. Without them the switch (zerus-5wmh.13) loses notifications.

Qt's behaviour is the parity target:
- **Posting:** UNUserNotificationCenter under the app's identity, with the default sound and one request per attention token (zerus.attention.<token>).
- **Clearing:** pending and delivered notifications are removed when the attention clears.
- **Clicking:** the default action opens that session's window.

Follow the desktop status contract in AGENTS.md:
- unread reply identity is kept;
- notifications for replies alone wait until the background work completes;
- native work and explicit attention take precedence;
- Mute and Reduce settings apply as in Qt.

Build a small native module, spec row 290, rather than tauri-plugin-notification. Request authorization the way Qt does. Under the switch bundle's identity (the Mac switch slice under zerus-5wmh.12), the existing grant carries over when the designated requirement matches.

Linux notifications remain separate work.

title: Tauri client: Mac switch bundle that takes over Zerus.app (com.hgdev.hgs-tray), installed through mac-install.sh
description:
The macOS part of phase 7, pulled forward for the switch. Owner decisions of 2026-10-28 are recorded on zerus-5wmh.13:
- The new client takes over Qt's identity, com.hgdev.hgs-tray, as Zerus.app.
- Qt is removed at the switch, and all its data and drafts are kept. Rollback means reinstalling Qt.
- Only the new client starts at login.

This bead covers the Mac only. Arch stays on Qt.

Bundle
- Contents/Info.plist matches Qt's: CFBundleIdentifier com.hgdev.hgs-tray, CFBundleName Zerus, CFBundleExecutable hgs-tray (Tauri mainBinaryName) and LSUIElement.
- The tray LaunchAgent template ships in Contents/Resources/setup, as scripts/package-macos.py installs it for Qt.
- The dev app keeps dev.zerus.next and its own name.
- scripts/check-macos-bundle.py and its tests accept the Tauri bundle.

Signing and identity
- Sign with the identity the installed Qt carries, following the continuity rules in tray/sign-local-macos.py:
  - Developer ID Application or Apple Development;
  - the same team;
  - no requirement that pins a cdhash.
- Release signing goes through scripts/sign-macos.py: hardened runtime and the entitlements the client needs, notarisable in the macos-signing environment.
- TCC grants and the Notification Center identity key on the bundle id and the designated requirement. Before the switch, compare `codesign -d -r-` of the new bundle with the installed Qt's on the Mac, and report the result to the coordinator.
  - If they are equal, the grants carry over.
  - If they differ, the grants will be asked for again. An Apple Development certificate, for example, pins the leaf certificate's name.

Updater contract (tray/update-installed.py, unchanged)
- `--build-info` prints Qt's JSON shape, including the version and the Dev number.
- `tell application id "com.hgdev.hgs-tray" to quit` and SIGTERM flush drafts, then exit.
- The single-instance socket and its show/sessions lines come from the menu-bar bead. The updater finds the old socket path and waits on it for the new GUI.
- The updater's draft check keeps passing. zerus-5wmh.12.1 adds the client's own drafts root.

Qt's stores are read as they are and never rewritten
- The files:
  - ~/Library/Preferences/com.hgdev.hgs-tray.plist (QSettings, organization hgdev, application hgs-tray);
  - its .drafts folder;
  - ~/Library/Application Support/hgdev/hgs-tray.
- The plist is also the new bundle's NSUserDefaults domain. List what Cocoa or WebKit writes there, and check that Qt's keys stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The switch snapshots the plist beside the rollback copy.
- The client keeps its private data in its own directory.
- Decide in the plan whether the client's data directory follows the bundle id or is pinned, and what happens to durable drafts typed in the dev app.

Switch flow
- The switch runs only through mac-install.sh and tray/update-installed.py: draft quit, flush, snapshot and verify.
- The build carries the main CI sequence as ZERUS_DEV_BUILD_NUMBER. It never replaces a numbered Dev install with an unnumbered build.
- The one rollback copy is the last Qt bundle. Add a rollback command that reinstalls exactly that copy, and document it in docs/macos-distribution.md and client/README.md.
- The switch never touches:
  - the hgs CLI;
  - the hgs-recovery and hgs-voice agents;
  - native agents or tmux;
  - the mobile connector.
- Installing on the owner's Mac stays with the coordinator.

title: WebKitGTK display link: match the monitor without millimetres and pace without DRM vblank (upstream patch)
description: Owner request 2026-10-28: a separate session (Kimi) prepares WebKitGTK patches. title: Tauri client: evaluate the CEF (Chromium) runtime on Linux for full display rate

Measure Chromium/CEF frame pacing on the owner's 144 Hz KDE Wayland NVIDIA desktop with the existing harness, and report size, packaging, security update cadence, IPC/COOP-COEP compatibility and integration cost. Feature work and releases do not wait for it.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text:
Findings 2026-10-28 (research and headless spike; real-display numbers follow in the next comment).
Prior art: nobody has made WebKitGTK pace above 60 Hz on NVIDIA. WebKit bug 325789 (2026-09-30, NEW, no patch) is exactly our KWin/NVIDIA mm mismatch (GDK 597x336 vs DRM 600x340); bug 199376 c9 reports drmWaitVBlank EOPNOTSUPP on the open NVIDIA driver; GTK issue 8461 reports that a GTK 3 window drawn with GL never requests wl_surface.frame on Wayland, so its frame clock stays at 60 Hz (a likely third gate for webkit2gtk-4.1). WPE uses the same DRM lookup. Projects that got past 60 Hz left WebKitGTK (GNOME-Turntable to GTK 4 GL, tuxbooks to Electron). The Tauri linux-graphics page mentions frame rate once ("low frame rates in WebGL heavy views", software paths), never refresh rate or 60 Hz pacing; its links (tauri#9394, WebKit 261874, NVIDIA forum 274741) do not mention frame rate.
Tauri CEF runtime: active on branch v3 (78f49ba, 2026-10-21): tauri 3.0.0-alpha.5, tauri-runtime-cef 3.0.0-alpha.6 pinned to cef =154.5.0 (CEF 154.0.34, Chromium 154.0.8037.98; CEF no longer updates M154, current CEF is 156.0.14). feat/cef (9d1a5b1, 2026-10-07, tauri 2.11.5, cef =151.8.1) is the older line; v3 holds all of it but one macOS fix. All active Linux CEF PRs target v3 (#16294, #16352, #16210, #16242, #16338; OSR #16225 merged). The runtime forces X11 (runtime.rs 3326 and 3336): XWayland only on KDE Wayland; CEF has no native Wayland embedding (cef#2804).
Port: our zerus-client crate builds and runs on tauri-runtime-cef v3 with four edits (cef_entry_point on main, .runtime(Cef), display.rs on the GTK 4 API, Cargo deps); raw next_batch (ArrayBuffer), invoke and COOP/COEP (crossOriginIsolated true, 5 us timer) work unchanged. Keeping macOS on WKWebView means the whole client on Tauri 3 alpha (macOS on tauri-runtime-wry v3) or two tauri majors behind cfg.
Blockers: every Tauri-CEF Linux app idles one core at 100% (tauri#16189, open, no PR; Chromium's MessagePumpGlib work source stays attached under external_message_pump); the spike's local patch brings idle to 0.4%. The Chrome-style profile picks up system Chromium external extensions (Plasma Browser Integration) and makes outbound requests even with --disable-extensions. Open keyboard/focus issues: #16251, #16351, #16249.
Costs (Xvfb, not representative): about 309 MiB installed (stripped libcef.so 272 MB, en-US only), 103-108 MiB compressed; first contentful paint 1.6-1.7 s cold, 0.8-1.1 s warm; idle PSS 568 MiB for the ported client (13 processes); IPC p50 0.6 ms for 1 KiB, 2.5 ms for 1 MiB. CEF security fixes reach a CEF build 1.4-5 days after Chrome; each needs a cef-rs and runtime bump (exact pin) and our rebuild.
Electron 45.1 (Chromium 156) runs natively on Wayland by default, but the Rust core moves to a napi-rs addon or a sidecar.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text:
Real display, arch, 2026-10-28 07:33-07:49 UTC (two 144 Hz outputs, scale 1, RTX 3090 Ti, nvidia 615.78.08 vblank=N), synthetic harness, 3 x 10 s runs, worst counts, T 6.94 ms:
- Tauri v3 + CEF 154 spike (with the #16189 fix), XWayland (forced by the runtime): every pacing scenario passes criterion 1. Worst-run means 6.95-6.96 ms, 1438-1440 frames per 10 s, no interval above 2.5 T, none in the 60 Hz band. GPU compositing on through ANGLE OpenGL on the NVIDIA GPU. Session open median 71.8 ms, input to frame 0.33 ms, idle tree 0.5% CPU, PSS 720 MiB.
- cefsimple CEF 156 with a native X11 parent (Tauri's mode), XWayland: all pass, means 6.95-6.98 ms.
- Chrome 155 native Wayland: four pass (6.94-6.96 ms); activity-scroll worst run 7.05 ms fails the mean bound narrowly.
- Reference: WebKitGTK 2.54.1 on the same display 16.04-16.07 ms (zerus-5wmh.14).
So Chromium reaches 144 Hz on this desktop, including through XWayland on NVIDIA without DRM vblank.
Keyboard and focus, automated (private Xvfb, no WM; XTEST keys; activation emulated with XSetInputFocus + WM_TAKE_FOCUS + _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW; decoy window focused before start; logger in a copy of client/dist reporting through perf_log; seven steps incl. setxkbmap ru): Tauri 2 WebKitGTK client 7/7 in 4 runs. Tauri v3 CEF client 2/7 in 3 runs: keys reach the page only after a click inside the web content; after any window activation (start, switch back) every key is lost (tauri#16251, #16351). With tauri PR #16352 applied: 4, 3, 0, 4, 4 of 7 in 5 runs: switching back works in most runs, startup input still lost, one run lost all input even after clicks. Limits: no KWin, no real Alt+Tab, Xvfb instead of XWayland.

comments.text: Live clients on the arch display, 2026-10-28 08:10-08:27 UTC, main 1f388605, live data, ZERUS_CLIENT_PERF=auto, back to back: CEF client (Tauri v3, XWayland) paces at 144 Hz on live data (medians 6.93-7.04 ms; 3 of 5 scenarios pass every criterion, transform and left each had one run with a slow-frame tail); WebKitGTK client 16-17.7 ms. title: Drive task state from execution attempts and an explicit session queue
description: Introduce revision-scoped execution attempts, confirmed executor session/native-child identities, a deterministic lifecycle reducer and a durable per-executor foreground queue independent of the GUI. Separate submission, acceptance, begin, progress, ready and result evidence; serialize tasks for one session, expose true parallel executors, handle yield/handoff/reopen/cancel and reject late reports from previous generations. Native Stop must pause dispatch, never imply completion or trigger automatic resume. Extend CLI and desktop/mobile typed views compatibly.

Owner clarification 2026-10-26: Pause on a card must pause that task, not every task assigned to its session. Implement execution accounting first; do not expose a session-wide interrupt as task pause. Cards should have stage-appropriate primary actions once their execution semantics are supported.
Inspector follow-up adds persisted executor plans, exact new-session launch correlation with local reserved delivery, current native-child/dispatch binding and idempotent active-start acknowledgement. Reservations are per desktop, not a distributed execution lease; full revision/attempt accounting, stale report guards, scheduler and true per-task pause remain open.

title: Make manual worktree process consent usable across unrelated SSH churn
description: Found during zerus-gxlu using two read-only reviews of the retained checkout. Worktree fingerprints were identical, but the exact process consent SHA-256 changed only because one protected sshd-session outside the CLI invocation ancestry was replaced by another. Current removal would reject that unchanged folder before Git. Review the scope and lifetime of explicit manual uncertainty acceptance so normal unrelated host process churn does not create an endless reconfirmation loop. Keep automatic cleanup conservative, preserve known process/session occupants and ownership/file protections, and do not whitelist process names or stop unrelated system services. Explain the specific blocker and a supported next action. Compare Orca ownership-scoped PTY teardown as design evidence, without copying its destructive defaults.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed design defines bounded manual consent for process uncertainty, retains all automatic and known-use protections, and covers changed unreadable process sets and local versus SSH launch paths. The UI exposes a meaningful recovery action. Exact historical screenshot attribution remains separate from the reproduced mechanism.
notes:
Implemented v2 manual uncertainty acceptance bound to repository and unchanged checkout fingerprint/ownership for five minutes on the owning computer. Fresh complete process inventory is still required; known use, sessions, ownership/file changes and all other blockers remain protected. Unrelated protected PID replacement does not invalidate accepted uncertainty. Automatic cleanup never consumes this token. Removed the obsolete PID-roster confirmation helper, retaining diagnostic process identities and invocation ancestry. Tests prove expiry/future timestamps/repository or checkout replacement, actual protected process replacement, separate protected launchers, known process and session blockers, and ignored-data consent. Documentation and both agent instruction files updated. Local source and Linux qualification complete; installed CLI and GUI were not replaced.

title: Recover worktree cleanup after definite pre-removal refusals
description: Found during zerus-gxlu on main f077cfab. WorktreeBatchCleanupDialog sets m_started permanently on the first removal attempt. A native stale process-consent refusal returns before Git removal, but the UI reports Not confirmed, disables file inspection, and offers only Close despite asking for another review. Distinguish definite refusal before deletion from an unknown deletion outcome. Provide a visible fresh review action for remaining folders, keep inspection accessible, require renewed scoped consent when evidence changes, and keep removed targets and uncertain requests out of retry. Use structured native outcome data rather than authorizing replay from arbitrary error text.
acceptance_criteria: A stale-consent refusal visibly says the folder was kept, allows fresh checking and inspection in the same flow, and requires new explicit removal consent. A lost or unknown removal result never enables replay. Completed batch targets are never resubmitted.
notes:
Owner approved the proposed lifecycle on 2026-10-26: one termination confirmation, background cleanup, clear removed/kept/unknown results, same-flow recheck and file inspection, details on demand, and usable bounded manual process uncertainty consent. Preserve branches, conversations, automatic safety and uncertain-operation no-replay.

title: Review worktree cleanup dead end and compare Orca lifecycle
description: Investigate the owner screenshot where confirmed cleanup ends with a stale process confirmation and no next action. Read current Zerus cleanup UI and native guards, compare the current upstream stablyai/orca worktree creation, archive, deletion, restore and local-data behavior, and provide source-backed findings with concrete UX recommendations. This task is investigation; preserve live folders, sessions and services.
notes:
Investigation completed against Zerus main f077cfab and pinned stablyai/orca 4a37a6b95285993db56e77442bad43beb898b638 on 2026-10-26. Current read-only reviews of the retained checkout had identical worktree fingerprints; process_fingerprint changed solely because an unrelated protected sshd-session outside invocation ancestry was replaced. Both SHA-256 proofs were independently reproduced from returned JSON. This proves a current failure mechanism, not exact historical screenshot causality. The native stale-consent error returns before Git removal. The GUI labels this definite refusal Not confirmed, permanently disables removal and inspection with m_started, and offers no fresh review. Follow-up bugs zerus-iqaz and zerus-1umo capture the two verified defects. Existing zerus-k403 already covers partial Git deregistration leaving invisible folder leftovers.

Orca comparison: its primary entity is a named workspace containing a checkout and terminals. Create uses a selectable repo base/start ref, background setup, optional shared ignored paths and .worktreeinclude copies. Delete confirmation closes at acceptance and workspace rows own progress; native removal stops workspace-owned PTYs under watcher fences and uses Git. The inspected deletion path has no equivalent all-user cwd/executable inventory. Default modal confirmation sets forceOnConfirm=true, allowing tracked/untracked discard after its disclosure; this does not itself waive strict PTY-stop proof. Always Force Delete is a separate opt-in that may waive that proof. Branch removal normally follows checkout removal, preserving uncertain branches for a separate review; squash equivalence may also qualify branch cleanup. Failed background removals retain durable records and explicit retry paths even after Git deregistration. Interrupted accepted removals may resume automatically on restart, unlike Zerus uncertain-removal policy. Sources: docs/site/content/docs/model/worktrees.mdx; renderer sidebar DeleteWorktreeDialog.tsx and delete-worktree-failure-toast.tsx; main ipc/worktrees/removal/remove-registered-local-worktree.ts and worktree-removal-ownership.ts; main git/worktree-branch-removal.ts; main worktree-background-removal.ts.

Recommendation for owner review: preserve session archive and retained branches, use one termination consent with background progress, show definite results Folder removed / Folder kept with a reason / Result unknown, reveal relevant file changes or local data on demand, and provide same-flow fresh checking after definite refusal. Process uncertainty needs usable scoped manual consent; automatic cleanup and known occupant protections remain strict. Do not solve this by whitelisting service names or stopping unrelated services. No application code changes, live deletion, installed update, commit or push performed.
close_reason: Source-backed Orca comparison and read-only diagnosis completed. Confirmed two separate cleanup defects and filed zerus-iqaz and zerus-1umo; application changes remain future work.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: Source result (not delivered, not pushed): commit bc6e7176 (tree 73bc4b68) on local branch mac/activity-scroll-pvfa8 from a5b0967d; tray/src/MarkdownObjects.cpp (+7) and tray/tests/test_markdownobjects.cpp (+39). Installed GUI (provenance 3a69386d, verified running hash) has the same Activity renderer as main, so this was a source bug, not a deployment gap. Verified cause at 2x: QPainter toggles antialiasing around every text item under a scaling transform; each toggle makes the raster engine replay and rasterize the rounded chip clip, so the per-band chip text redraw in paintChips dominated (sample: drawTextItem -> replayClipOperations -> clip path rasterization). Fix: preset antialiasing before the clip for bands without selected or found text. Synthetic Cyrillic many-short-pill reply, offscreen DPR2 with CoreText fonts: full repaint p90 55.5 -> 7.3 ms, max 58.9 -> 7.8 ms, median 9.9 -> 6.1 ms; DPR1 unchanged; 10 of 10 pixel captures byte-identical (DPR1/DPR2, with and without selection). New relative regression test fails on unfixed source (3614 ms at 2x vs 66 ms at 1x for 20 frames) and passes fixed. Residual: a selection across dense pills still costs about 99 ms per DPR2 frame, unchanged before and after; follow-up proposed. Root verifies acceptance and delivery.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: Correction to bc6e7176's pixel claim, from reading Qt 6.11.2 source (not yet compiled or verified): QTextLine::draw_internal defers underline, strikeout and overline and draws them at the end of each line with the painter's current antialiasing. Before bc6 those lines inside pills were aliased at 2x; with the preset they are antialiased. Affects only struck-out text inside pills (Markdown ~~...~~, including code spans) in bands without a selection; links have no underline. Proposed amendment: skip the preset for blocks with decorated fragments, cached in the chip index. Also proposed (read-only, awaiting root GO): an exact two-pass separation for selection and find bands, non-glyph output forwarded with antialiasing off and glyphs forwarded with it preset, under stated qualifying conditions and byte-exact oracles. The selection residual is about 99 ms per 2x frame today.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin

title: Design verified computer pairing and end-to-end encrypted session payloads
description: Audit 2026-10-18: API v1 is TLS-only and the relay can read snapshots, requests and results (services/mobile/README.md). No design document covers verified computer pairing or end-to-end encryption. Required before promising that a cloud operator cannot read customer content; the open self-hostable protocol must be preserved.
design: Final reviewed design: docs/encrypted-workspaces.md and services/mobile/crypto/README.md define pairwise RFC9180 HPKE X25519/HKDF-SHA256/AES256GCM plus strict Ed25519 signatures; separate endpoint keys, typed secret-bound candidate proof, invitation-pinned bootstrap, signed linear membership with durable head history and immutable device bindings. Revocation is computer-signed; re-enrollment/rotation uses a new device identity. Per-recipient ciphertext, permanent request tombstones, exact persisted retries and protected local journals preserve no-replay. Relay keeps routing/queues/receipts/push/quotas and bounded service metadata; decryption ends at the trusted gateway before existing authenticated SSH. APIv1 remains explicit plaintext with no protected fallback. Recipient-compromise forward secrecy, global consensus, guaranteed freshness/availability and remote erasure are not promised.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed design document covering key verification, payload encryption, key rotation, multi-device and protocol compatibility, with owner approval before implementation.
notes:

title: A failed model/effort change blocks every later settings change and the first message
description: When a native settings change (model or effort) is not confirmed, effort.rs marks input_pending_at=now. Only a later native event (last_event_at > pending) clears it. A Claude /model attempt that fails without switching emits no hook event, so a quiet or fresh session stays blocked: every later settings attempt fails with 'previous input has not been confirmed by the agent', and first_message_candidate becomes false, so the first message is blocked too. Fix: record a settings-specific marker. It blocks only while Terminal is not verifiably back at an empty recognized prompt; message input_pending_at semantics stay unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: After an unconfirmed settings change whose Terminal is back at an empty agent prompt, a new settings request and the first/next message are accepted. While Terminal still shows the picker or a draft, both stay blocked. No keys are ever replayed for the same request ID.
notes:
Implemented on branch fix/settings-unconfirmed-and-auto-mode: failed settings mark settings_unconfirmed_at only when typed keys were not visibly read or Terminal is not back at the empty prompt; it blocks settings/messages until a native event and no longer touches input_pending_at/first-message state. Tests: tests/test_claude_settings.py, tests/test_settings.py, input.rs unit test. Not compiled locally (no Rust/Qt/tmux on the Windows dev box); needs CI.

title: Clipped Claude approval panels in detached 80x24 panes cannot be answered from Activity
description: Owner report 2026-10-17 (macOS GUI): a Bash dangerous-rm safety approval with a long command showed only Open Terminal: "Zerus cannot read this approval completely. Enlarge Terminal or answer it there." Root cause: the session had no attached client, so its tmux pane kept the default 80x24 size. Claude draws the approval panel taller than the pane and keeps no scrollback for it (history_size 0 with Claude 2.1.296), so the title and the start of the command show nowhere and claude_approval::parse refuses. Same root cause as zerus-0yrj (AskUserQuestion).

title: Windows desktops whose whole session is in a job cannot start local sessions
description: Reported 2026-10-17 (Zerus 0.44.0, hgs 1.53.0, Windows 11 Home 26H2 build 26300): every process of the interactive session, explorer.exe included, is in a job; hgs-tray.exe started from Explorer cannot start a host (ClientError::InJob). CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB succeeds but the child stays in a job, so an outer job forbids breakaway. D4 refuses a host in any job, so local sessions never start on such a desktop. Proposal (needs the reporter's job data first): accept a host whose own job also holds the desktop shell (GetShellWindow's process in JobObjectBasicProcessIdList), since such sessions then end no earlier than the desktop, which docs already state; keep refusing every other job (agent sandboxes, terminals, CI steps). Also name the remedy in the desktop error, and review that the GUI's PTY and swarm-worker kill-on-close jobs lack BREAKAWAY_OK.
close_reason: Merged in #203 (29dc8a0f): a host whose job also holds the desktop shell is accepted (desktop_job); reproduced and verified on the Windows dev PC. GUI PTY and swarm-worker jobs follow in zerus-tft0.

title: iOS #0: foundation, project and Dev build installed on the test iPhone
description:
Sub-project #0 of the iOS epic: create mobile/ios, build it and install Dev builds on the test iPhone attached to the Mac, with a walking skeleton that proves networking, Keychain and signing on a real device.

Next step: finish the brainstorming for #0 with the owner (questions below, one at a time), present the design, write docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-ios-foundation-design.md, get owner review, then writing-plans.

Environment verified 2026-10-16: arm64 Mac, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), iOS 26.0 simulator runtime. Test iPhone 11 Pro on iOS 26.0 is paired and connected (xcrun devicectl list devices). A valid Apple Development certificate of the owner's paid team is in the login keychain and Xcode has an Apple ID account, so automatic signing with -allowProvisioningUpdates should work. A Developer ID Application certificate exists for macOS casks; there is no Apple Distribution certificate yet (needed by #9). xcodegen, fastlane and tuist are not installed; Homebrew lives in /opt/homebrew and is only on the login-shell PATH (use zsh -lc over ssh). About 54 GB disk free (88 percent used): keep DerivedData in one dedicated bounded location.

Open questions for the owner:
(a) Bundle ID, durable once an App Store record exists. Candidate: app.zerus.mobile, identical to the Android applicationId, one app ID shared by Dev/TestFlight/Stable as Android shares one package.
(b) Minimum iOS version. Proposal: iOS 17.
(c) Meaning of Dev. Proposal: a locally built, development-signed build installed on the attached iPhone by a script; TestFlight internal testing becomes the Dev channel in #9.

Proposed design (not yet approved):
- mobile/ios/Zerus.xcodeproj using Xcode file-system synchronized groups (objectVersion 77), so the project file stays small and new sources are picked up from folders; no generator dependency.
- A SwiftUI app target, a testable core module (protocol models, RelayClient, credential store) and unit tests runnable on the simulator.
- mobile/ios/DEV_VERSION (marketing base) plus a build number from the CI sequence; local builds embed source commit and dirty state and never claim a CI number.
- mobile/ios/scripts/dev-install.sh on the Mac: xcodebuild with automatic signing and -allowProvisioningUpdates, dedicated -derivedDataPath, install with xcrun devicectl device install app, launch with devicectl device process launch. A Linux-side wrapper rsyncs a worktree's mobile/ios to a Mac scratch directory over ssh -o BatchMode=yes and runs it, so agents on Arch can build uncommitted work.
- Walking skeleton: pairing (POST /v1/pair, credential in Keychain, HTTPS only, zerus://pair link prefill with explicit confirmation), GET /v1/capabilities, GET /v1/computers list, and the read-only demo.
- CI: a macOS job on a standard runner that builds for the simulator without signing and runs the unit tests, wired into the existing ci.yml gate.
- Docs: mobile/ios/README.md (build and install), README.md mobile section, docs/mobile-architecture.md status line.

Remaining for this task: install on the test iPhone once Xcode on the Mac has a signed-in Apple ID of the team (or an App Store Connect API key is provided); then dev-install.sh needs no further changes.

title: iOS client with Android feature parity (native SwiftUI)
description:
Goal (owner, 2026-10-16): build the iOS version of the Zerus mobile client, learn to build and install Dev builds on the test iPhone attached to the Mac, then produce TestFlight/App Store builds.

Owner decisions from the 2026-10-16 brainstorming (superpowers brainstorming, architectural path):
1. Scope: full feature parity with the Android client, not an MVP.
2. Approach A: a separate native Swift/SwiftUI client under mobile/ios. Port logic from the Kotlin client; do not refactor Android. Keep subtle contracts aligned with shared JSON contract fixtures exercised by both Android and iOS tests (existing examples: mobile/android/app/src/test/resources/session-filter-contract.json and optional-question-contract.json). Rejected: B (Kotlin Multiplatform shared logic + SwiftUI) and C (Compose Multiplatform); both require restructuring the working Android app.
3. Decompose into sub-projects; each gets its own spec, plan and implementation (brainstorming -> written spec in docs/superpowers/specs -> owner review -> writing-plans -> execution). Order: #0 foundation and Dev build, then #9 TestFlight/App Store distribution immediately after #0, then #1 sessions and machines, #2 conversation, #3-#7 in parallel, #8 notifications.

State at handoff: classification, scope, approach and decomposition are approved. The #0 design is not yet approved; its open questions are listed in the #0 child. No spec, plan or code exists yet.

Reading list: docs/mobile-architecture.md (Protocol version 1 table, Trust and authorization, Delivery safety, Notifications, Public distribution), services/mobile/relay/README.md, mobile/android/README.md, mobile/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerus/mobile/ (about 20k lines; RelayApi.kt, ZerusViewModel.kt, MainActivity.kt are the entry points), mobile/android/app/src/test, docs/public-distribution.md (Dev version rule), docs/macos-distribution.md (Apple credentials, macos-signing environment), docs/ci-and-aur.md, CONTRIBUTING.md.

Constraints (AGENTS.md): keep API v1 and durable request identities compatible; no credentials or login material in the repository; free standard GitHub runners only; SHA-pinned actions; Apple credentials stay in the main-only macos-signing environment; never auto-merge; mirror instruction changes in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; Dev builds use next-version-dev.N.

iOS-specific facts: CFBundleShortVersionString must be at most three integers, so the -dev.N suffix cannot be part of the marketing version; carry the Dev sequence in CFBundleVersion and show X.Y.Z-dev.N in About. The relay accepts only provider fcm in POST /v1/push today; iOS needs APNs either directly from the relay or through FCM for iOS (decide in #8). The Android in-app updater does not apply on iOS; distribution is TestFlight/App Store.
Unassigned so far: Firebase diagnostics and usage analytics parity (docs/mobile-architecture.md Firebase diagnostics) and third-party notices; decide during #9 together with the privacy manifest.

title: Claude child StopFailure keeps the parent Working forever
description: A Claude workflow child that ends with StopFailure (for example rate_limit 'weekly limit') is saved as state=working with display_state=unknown and never receives SubagentStop. Counters report it as unknown (subagent_active_count 0), but telemetry::child_working() checks only state==working, so Stop and settle_children keep the parent phase=working and all idle-only actions (pause, fork, effort, clear, compact) stay blocked. Observed 2026-10-16 on arch: session builds idle at the native prompt since its end_turn, shown as Working for 15+ hours; the workflow journal records type=failed for that agent and its transcript ends with a synthetic isApiErrorMessage rate_limit row. Needs owner direction on status semantics: proposal is to settle the child as finished with an error outcome when the hook reports StopFailure or the workflow journal records failed, and never let an unknown child establish current work.
close_reason: Merged in PR #184 (3120b6f8): Claude child StopFailure or workflow failure settles as error; unknown children never keep the parent working; stale records repaired on read.

title: Swarm controller loops on run_groups and disables conflict review
description: Commit 7406d595 added run_groups to SessionOrganization::toJson(), but SwarmController::presentation() copies only default_project, runs and imported_machines from the local organization. Every SessionsWindow rebuild re-adds run_groups through observe(), saveOrganization() calls SwarmController::edit(), m_desired differs from m_base, the controller sends a no-op swarm apply, presentation() drops run_groups again and organizationReady triggers another rebuild. Observed on mac Dev773 (2026-10-16): the persisted swarm/observedOrganization lacks run_groups while workspace/organization has it, and only 'hgs swarm apply' calls (no 5 s polls) were seen. Because settled() is false most of the time, SwarmDialog calls review->setBusy(true) every 200 ms and the conflict choices table is disabled, so the owner cannot select a value. The round trip also wipes run_groups, so archived run placement can be lost. Fix: preserve run_groups as local-only data in presentation() and add a regression test that a rebuild with run_groups settles without apply.
close_reason: Merged in PR #183 (f3590735): SwarmController::presentation keeps run_groups, so Sessions rebuilds no longer loop through swarm apply and conflict choices stay selectable.

title: Mobile delivery fixture test leaves account refreshes running and hangs Python 3.12 teardown
description: CI #721 (0d962407) Rust relay job hit its 25-minute deadline: after test_only_the_gateway_advertises_and_its_snapshot_reports_the_value printed ok, asyncio logged 'Close running child process: kill' and unittest never continued. Reproduced locally with CPython 3.12.13 and the CI package install: every snapshot starts an AccountCache.refresh task; the test closed only the journal, so IsolatedAsyncioTestCase teardown cancelled refresh, create_subprocess_exec and the transport's _connect_pipes together; the spawn cleanup then waits forever in Runner._cancel_all_tasks for an exit that needs connected pipes. Fix: await the peer and root AccountCache.close() before closing the journal, as Connector.run shutdown and other connector tests do.
close_reason: Frozen fixture-only correction retained in exact4e2c0c3e; affected complete hosted CI722 passed, and the combined Dev722 wave is installed/publicly verified. No production change from this fix.

Only services/mobile/tests/test_mobile_delivery.py changes (+6). File sha256 ea89406370f1cda67428e8fc21ba50893e79de88e580927ce467a3e4a9a3852c, equal to graph's reviewed immutable snapshot. Evidence (CPython 3.12.13, CI-equivalent venv with `pip install ./services/mobile -r services/mobile/tests/requirements.txt`):

This matches CI #721 job 116733340754.

After 5 s, create_subprocess_exec and refresh are still pending. Cancelling _connect_pipes together with the spawn leaves the exit waiter unresolved, because exit waiters need all pipes connected and then disconnected.
- With the fix, 0 tasks remain at teardown for all 5 tests in the module, and they pass.

title: Rust connector runtime core: HTTP client, native layer, loops and reads
description: Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-rust-mobile-connector-design.md, slice C2. HTTP client (hyper + rustls with native roots, HTTP/1.1, no proxy/redirects, Content-Type application/json, Content-Length, identity encoding), spawn gate (macOS only), native layer with timeouts and output caps, claim/heartbeat/result loops, capability probe, read operations; ported black-box modules move to ported.json as they pass in Rust mode. Decisions carried in from H2-H4 and C1 reviews: implement the test hooks ZERUS_CONNECTOR_TEST_NATIVE_TIMEOUT and ZERUS_CONNECTOR_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE (names fixed in connector_harness.py); a receipt within MAX_RESULT whose canonical form with request_id exceeds 1 MiB uploads as uncertain with result null and a fixed error; a non-string or over-4096-code-point native error becomes a fixed text; stderr above 8 MiB fails the native call as in Python (read under the cap, content discarded); the generic 'connector could not record native outcome' receipts pinned by test_bb_worktrees and the gigaam-device-list vector are reproduced unless recorded as reviewed divergences; Rust retires a stored result the relay keeps refusing (divergence a) per test_bb_native_limits; the relay refuses canonical receipts over 1 MiB or errors over 4096 code points, so Python's journaled oversized receipts block later claims (pinned as Python behaviour).
close_reason: Merged in PR #139: the Rust connector runs as a real connector for reads (inspect, process_output, mark_read, history, catalog, dirs, worktrees) with hyper/rustls HTTP, the native layer, heartbeat and claim loops, divergences a/b/g/h and test hooks; other operations are refused and never advertised until C3-C6. ported.json runs check, computer, heartbeat, inspection_bounds, journal, runtime and startup in Rust mode. Review fixed a provider-timestamp panic, a pinned wait=1 poll after a cleared refusal, a Duration panic and quadratic bound_inspection.

title: Start the shared tmux server outside the unit that first needs it
description: Found by the zerus-nbzl.2 rehearsal (2026-10-15, systemd 262, tmux 3.8 built with libsystemd): tmux puts every pane created by a client inside a systemd unit into a tmux-spawn-<uuid>.scope with PartOf=<the unit holding the tmux server> and SendSIGHUP=yes. When that unit is stopped, systemd also stops these pane scopes, so the tmux server exits after its last pane, even with KillMode=process. Whatever unit first starts the shared default tmux server (a desktop-launched GUI unit, hgs-tray.service, zerus-mobile-connector.service, a worker) therefore owns all agent panes: stopping it, or a graphical logout when it is PartOf graphical-session.target, can end every native agent. Start the shared tmux server in its own transient scope (systemd-run --user --scope, as the DeepSeek and opencode hosts already do) whenever hgs has to create it, verify with systemctl --user show -p ConsistsOf, and rehearse only on isolated tmux sockets. Never restart or stop live units to test this.
notes: PR #126 (fix/tmux-server-own-scope), reviewed; awaiting CI.
close_reason: Merged in PR #126: on Linux inside a user unit with a reachable user manager, hgs starts a new shared tmux server in its own hgs-tmux-<uuid> scope (systemd-run --user --scope --collect), so stopping the launching unit no longer ends agent panes; running servers are never touched; refused scopes fall back to the plain command. CI ran the new integration test on ubuntu-24.04 (3 pass, PartOf control skipped: runner tmux lacks systemd).

title: Prevent default Inbox observation from racing explicit project assignment
description: A newly observed session can be published into the local default project while another desktop explicitly assigns the same exact machine/session to its selected project. Verified catalog history contains two concurrent parentless session assignments at the same clock: the observing host chose ungrouped while the launching desktop chose the selected project. A later explicit write merged both parents and restored the intended project. Passive observation must not compete with an explicit launch or move. Preserve deliberate moves to the default project, exact launch/run/session identity, existing conflict review and compatibility with resident clients. Add a synthetic two-peer regression before choosing the protocol or presentation fix.
design: Keep first-observed session rows and their order in the local desktop organization with an unassigned_sessions marker. SwarmController removes those memberships from both initialize and apply payloads; explicit moves and verified launches remove the marker. Shared catalog membership wins over passive placement on refresh, including rename arrival ordering. New payloads carry the additive organization hint session_assignments_explicit so the CLI preserves unseen competing explicit choices instead of applying its legacy passive-observation guard. Older CLIs ignore that hint; shared operation schema, existing assignments/conflicts and unmarked historical caches are unchanged. Full race prevention requires updating observing desktops; the CLI update additionally preserves explicit first-choice conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: A remote session launched into an explicit project remains in that project when another GUI first observes it concurrently; passive fallback display does not create an authoritative competing assignment. Explicit moves to the default project remain synchronized. Existing and real conflicts are preserved for review.
notes:
2026-10-12 validation: the new desktop regression failed before the fix by exporting passive session membership. The fixed source passes all 53 Linux GUI targets and all 15 affected native macOS targets, 27 Swarm unit contracts on Rust 1.85, and 15 isolated real-CLI Swarm tests (14-suite run plus the added compatibility contract). Both observation/launch write orders converge without assignment conflicts; an unseen explicit first choice remains a reviewable conflict. The additive hint also passes against the retained pre-fix CLI binary without changing catalog operations. Source privacy/syntax/version checks and targeted rustfmt pass.
2026-10-12 final integration: the Inbox fix and composer feedback cleanup are reconciled with main 944f19e. Full Linux GUI build and all 53 CTest targets pass; native macOS GUI build and all 15 final integration targets pass, with all 314 staged GUI/build/test source files verified by SHA-256.
close_reason: Separate passive desktop placement from explicit shared assignment; preserve real conflicts and legacy catalog compatibility. Linux, native macOS and isolated two-peer CLI regressions pass.

title: Remove blocking draft writer barriers from navigation and send UI
description: Review zerus-pta0 against retained 0.41.0 release source: ComposerDraftStore::load and keys call global flushWrites; DraftWrites::flush and sync use BlockingQueuedConnection without a deadline. New-session selection, Saved drafts and explicit sending can therefore block the GUI behind unrelated slow disk writes despite asynchronous typing. A synthetic 400 ms writer delay makes loading an unrelated absent draft block the main thread 410 ms (0.13 ms thread CPU); queued GUI work cannot run. Use asynchronous draft loading and durable-send continuation with operation identity and fresh validation. Preserve atomic persistence before transport, draft recovery and no replay; do not bypass the durable barrier. Test navigation and explicit send while the writer remains stalled. Existing typing responsiveness coverage releases the writer before its send assertion.
design: Use one ordered worker with coalesced edit snapshots and noncoalescing durable operations. All GUI reads/index scans/writes use asynchronous continuations with exact key and revision. Loading may lock only its composer; navigation remains responsive. Pin accepted payload and target identity before durability, prevent duplicate sends, revalidate before transport, preserve recovery and no replay. Persist rename destination before retiring source. Normal widget destruction never globally drains; graceful application shutdown may drain.
notes: Implemented and reviewed asynchronous draft load/index/rename, ordered durable submission continuations, and bounded background attachment preparation/retry reads. Accepted payloads stay pinned to their original target across navigation; stale identity, failed persistence, missing retry receipt and expired unconsented cache prevent dispatch. Tests hold storage blocked while proving event-loop progress, navigation and zero premature transport; 22 integration outcome rows pass, including native Cocoa. Composer, question, attachment and SessionsWindow suites pass on macOS and Arch. User-selected attachment import remains synchronous within the reviewed scope. Qualified source change; installed GUI not updated.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed and qualified on macOS and Linux; source changes are ready for review, without deployment.

title: Bound Activity rendering latency and defer hidden transcript layout
description: Review zerus-pta0: ActivityView::render regenerates HTML and synchronously replaces and fully lays out the whole QTextDocument after one changed reply (ActivityView.cpp:1254-1264). SessionsWindow calls setTimeline even when Activity is hidden. Release Qt offscreen synthetic approximately 1 KB replies: 100 replies take 125-126 ms per change; 250 take 297-299 ms; 500 take 587-596 ms; hidden 500-reply updates take 580 ms. Identical snapshots are below 0.2 ms. This blocks all input on the shared GUI event loop. Implement bounded/incremental visible transcript work and defer hidden rendering while keeping data current. Preserve reading anchors, selection, exact history, clear boundaries and delivery identities. Add meaningful event-loop latency qualification for changed long histories and hidden panels; average idle CPU is insufficient.
design: Prepare journal HTML, source QTextDocument layout, cloned browser text and cursor-line geometry on one low-priority job per view. Qt setDocument invalidates an ordinary prepared document, so install a public QAbstractTextDocumentLayout adapter delegating draw, hit testing and geometry to the owned immutable source document; map selections by identical text positions and preserve image cursor metrics. Keep one active job plus the latest pending input. Separate presentation epochs from content revisions so same-conversation streaming makes progress without accepting stale session, search, theme or geometry results. Hidden views defer work. Commit preserves current selection and reading anchors. Each dedicated job thread parks after preparation until its document tree is retired: Qt FreeType destroys thread-local faces on thread exit despite live layout references, and sharing a working renderer thread with GUI paint could race font-engine caches. At application shutdown, drain preparation, delete documents while font resources remain alive, then stop and join threads before Qt GUI global teardown. Validate bounded thread retirement, interaction contracts and main-thread gaps through first paint, not setter time alone.
notes: Implemented and reviewed in isolated source worktree based on d8ceeab. HTML, full layout and cursor geometry run off the GUI thread; immutable layout adapter preserves selection, links and full history. Dedicated workers park until document retirement to preserve FreeType thread-local faces, with at most two workers per view. Hidden views defer work and streaming coalesces without starvation. Native Cocoa 500-reply changed snapshots: 21-27 ms GUI gaps including first paint, 1.18-1.26 s background preparation. Activity and SessionsWindow suites pass on macOS Qt 6.11.2 and Arch Qt 6.12.0. ASAN passes on both, including bounded worker retirement, pending shutdown and a separate live installed-document shutdown harness. Qualified source change; installed GUI not updated.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed and qualified on macOS and Linux; source changes are ready for review, without deployment.

title: Review desktop UI stalls under host load after performance fixes
description: Analyze main-thread responsiveness under general computer load, verify the installed version and remaining synchronous rendering or I/O paths, collect passive profiles and isolated synthetic measurements, and record prioritized findings. Audit only; preserve live native agents and user drafts.
notes:
Verified 2026-10-11: the live macOS process reports 0.41.0 and has a zerus-draft-writer thread; the checkout is 0.40.0 (05f0729). Reviewed the retained 0.41.0 release source archive. ActivityView.cpp and SessionList.cpp are byte-identical across the checkout and archive. Exact installed binary provenance is unconfirmed: its Mach-O UUID differs from the retained release build. An 8-second passive sample captures ActivityView::render -> setHtml/documentSize and whole-list/card painting on the main thread; fsync for ordinary draft edits is on the writer thread. No sustained total hang was captured. Isolated Release/Qt offscreen measurements with synthetic approximately 1 KB replies: changing one reply blocks setActivity for 125-126 ms with 100 replies, 297-299 ms with 250, and 587-596 ms with 500. Hidden Activity still costs 580 ms with 500 replies. Identical snapshots cost below 0.2 ms. With the existing write observer delaying only the draft worker 400 ms, loading an unrelated absent draft blocks the main thread 410 ms with only 0.13 ms thread CPU; a queued event does not run until return. Eight synthetic active rows at 2x scale repaint 25 times in two seconds (32 ms thread CPU); disabling activity animation produces zero paints in the same static fixture. These establish defects and avoidable work, not a complete attribution of the reported live freeze. Local diagnostic artifacts: /tmp/zerus-ui-review-harness and /tmp/zerus-ui-review-sample.txt. No application source edits, GUI/native restarts, live stress or publication.
Prioritized follow-ups: zerus-nug6 (P1 bounded Activity and hidden rendering), zerus-ts35 (P1 asynchronous draft barriers), zerus-3onx (P2 animation repaint regions). Review complete; the original live-load symptom remains unqualified until these paths are fixed and event-loop/input latency is measured under representative CPU and I/O pressure.
User clarified after the initial review: macOS; the entire interface stalls, including scrolling, switching sessions and all UI actions; typing makes the symptom especially apparent. This is a whole-window responsiveness report, not merely slow backend/session updates.
Typing-path follow-up, 2026-10-11: in retained 0.41.0 source, text/cursor signals enqueue asynchronous saves; draftChanged rebuilds the list only when draft presence changes, not on every character. The existing live sample also captures saveAsync -> directory -> QSettings construction -> QMacSettingsPrivate::sync -> CFPreferences on the GUI thread. This is residual native-settings work, not a demonstrated stall: 1000 synthetic native-format directory lookups measured median 0.0095 ms, p99 0.0147 ms and maximum 0.0868 ms. Do not attribute the reported freeze to this call without slow-episode evidence. The P1 Activity and blocking draft-barrier findings remain the strongest reproduced problems.
close_reason: Completed source review, passive live sampling and isolated Release Qt reproductions; recorded two P1 defects and a P2 rendering task. No claim that the live freeze is fixed.

acceptance_criteria: Reproduce and measure typing/event-loop latency under the reported workload on macOS; verify a targeted fix reduces it without losing crash-recoverable drafts, sending before durable persistence, reordering saved states, stealing focus, disrupting IME, or replaying uncertain delivery. Preserve per-session/subagent/question isolation and immutable attachment snapshots. Exercise relevant isolated Linux and macOS contracts.

title: Investigate intermittent process history cache recovery failure during release qualification
description: Release candidate 38142162351, exact source 9b8463dddfef568925c6795d538d5cafd8266e63: Linux Rust unit test state::processes::history::tests::incremental_recovery_caches_exact_completion_and_rejects_other_conversation failed at history.rs:227. Initial recovery succeeded; the immediate cached-receipt replay returned starting instead of failed. Investigate cache/lock behavior under parallel unit tests; keep publication gated on successful exact-source qualification.
notes: Verified reproduction: a concurrent child fork inherits the raw history-lock file descriptor, so closing the parent descriptor can leave the same flock alive until the child execs/exits. Private pre-exec fork contention reproduced the exact cached-receipt assertion on attempt 6, with try_lock_exclusive returning EAGAIN. Fix history recovery to use existing lock_until(..., Instant::now()) and its explicit-unlock Guard, preserving nonblocking polling. No live processes are involved. A fresh exact-source candidate is required before publication.
close_reason: Reproduced an inherited flock descriptor during concurrent fork/pre-exec (old code failed on probe 6 with EAGAIN at cached-receipt replay). History recovery now uses the existing nonblocking lock_until guard, whose explicit unlock releases the inherited flock. Full Rust unit suite passed 256 tests; 100 private fork-contention probes passed after the fix. Final release candidate will independently qualify this source.

title: Confirm cold context before submitting native question answers
description: A user submitted a desktop Claude question answer while the prompt cache was cold and received no context-cost warning or session action choice. The ordinary message composer has a cold-cache confirmation, but question submission must enforce the same explicit cost decision before native answer input. Preserve exact question/run/conversation identity, saved form drafts, no-replay receipts and read-only polling. Offer only context actions supported while a question is pending; do not clear or compact a live question implicitly. Add meaningful cancellation, confirmation and stale-modal regressions, review, publish and deploy under existing owner authorization.
design: Astra design: Desktop and Android native question answers use an explicit cold-cache cost choice before any sending state or transport. Offer Submit with full context and default Cancel; pending questions cannot use the ordinary message clear/compact continuation because those actions invalidate the answer. Capture the exact target, run/conversation, question identity/source/tool/schema, emitted answer payload and raw saved form/draft state. Revalidate identity, availability, unchanged draft and no existing pending/submitted/uncertain delivery after consent; same-schema polling is allowed. Guard reentrant dialogs and duplicate sends. Android retains only an in-memory confirmation intent across rotation, drops it on process restart and enforces the gate centrally in ViewModel.send so inline, expanded, approval and skip paths cannot bypass it. Preserve native no-replay receipts and exact form replacement mechanics.
notes:
Implemented and Astra-reviewed the desktop and Android common question-send cold-cache consent gates. Cancel preserves the complete saved form without creating delivery; consent pins exact target, question schema and raw draft. Android persistence-time expiry restores only its unchanged owned form and displays a question-local refusal. Final qualification: all 27 desktop modal scenarios; full 10 SessionsWindow shards, QuestionCard and HgsClient on Arch and Mac; Android plain Debug and Firebase Debug/Pilot each 519 tests with no failures, errors or skips, plus lint and signed/minified builds. All compiled source inputs match integrated main. Source syntax/version/privacy checks and Gitleaks tracked source/all Git history pass. GUI deployment and exact Android artifact emulator qualification/publication are pending.

title: Start hgs subprocesses without blocking the GUI thread
description: runHgs in tray/src/HgsClient.cpp starts about one hgs child per second (local ls every 2 s, peer ls over ssh, git-status, inspect, recovery, accounts) with QProcess on the GUI thread. On macOS Qt's vforkfd falls back to fork(), costing about 4 ms of main-thread time per launch in the large GUI process; Linux forks from the same thread.
acceptance_criteria: Launching and reaping hgs children no longer runs fork/exec on the GUI thread on macOS or Linux; timeouts, cancellation, ordering of results and error reporting stay unchanged; HgsClient tests pass.
notes: 2026-10-10: ProcessRunner owns all QProcess launches for runHgs, runWrite and requestRecovery on one worker thread (hgs-process-runner); results are queued to the owner on the GUI thread, owner destruction kills and reaps its children, a post routine reaps at exit; Linux uses UseVFork with Qt >= 6.7. GUI-thread cost per launch ~0.5 ms -> ~0.005 ms in a microbenchmark (the live profile showed ~4.2 ms fork). Residual on macOS: fork() takes malloc zone locks via atfork handlers, so a GUI allocation during a worker fork can still wait briefly; posix_spawn would avoid it. Branch perf/process-launch.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: full Qt suite passed on macOS (49/49) and Linux (48/48); in main as of b093ddb and installed on the Mac and arch on 2026-10-10.

title: Recovery jitter can exceed its 10% bound by a rounding error
description: recovery::schedule computed due_at as time + delay * (1.0 + jitter / 1000). For jitter 100, delay * 1.1 is not exact (90 * 1.1 = 99.00000000000001), so due_at exceeded the documented maximum and session_limits_wait_for_reset_and_interval_mode_uses_its_own_budget failed about once per 101 random job IDs (CI main for 6fd2598). Add the jitter separately.

title: Recovery keeps scheduling continuations while the agent is working
description: Observed with a Claude session on a rate-limited account: each recovery attempt goes dispatching -> retrying -> waiting within about 2 s because a new rate_limit provider hook arrives right after the continuation is delivered, while the agent stays busy/working and later answers (Claude appears to retry internally). Recovery reached attempt 11 and kept the panel at 'Waiting to retry (N attempts, repeats until stopped)' with the 'Limit reached' chip beside a working agent. Another Claude session on the same account received 11 queued '[HGS automatic recovery]' prompts in one user turn. Expected: a provider error followed by continued agent activity in the same turn must not schedule another continuation, the panel should not claim it is waiting to retry while the agent is working, and continuations must not queue up. Related: 2e28c15 reset-aware session limit recovery.
notes: Fix up as PR #56 (2026-10-14): accepted recovery episodes stay in progress while the agent keeps working; the account slot is released once the provider served the continuation (progress after the latest turn start). Root cause of the 11-attempt incidents was mostly a session limit read as rate limit, fixed earlier by 2e28c15.
close_reason: Merged in PR #56

title: Tauri client: flush read and attention marks on exit (bounded)
description:
Found in the organization final re-review (2026-10-28). Read marks and attention marks have no flush on RunEvent::Exit.

Tauri ends the process after Exit, so Attention's Drop never runs. A change made a few milliseconds before quitting can be lost: an invoke still in flight, a worker not yet woken, or one write in progress. The effect is that a reply shows unread again, or an attention mark reverts. An interrupted write leaves the old file intact.

Fix (client/src-tauri/src/lib.rs, the single Exit block):
- call Actions::flush_marks(), which is cheap and a no-op when nothing is unsaved;
- add a non-test attention flush with a time limit of about 500 ms to 1 s. Today's Attention::flush (actions.rs) is test-only and waits without a limit.

This matches Qt, whose read-mark store saves synchronously.

Part 2 target: on the Mac switch branch the call goes into crate::exit_work(app) (lifecycle::exit calls it before releasing the socket); on main without it, inside exit(app).

title: client/media: video_linux recording test fails under heavy load
description: a_test_recording_becomes_a_round_video_message failed once in the arch gate on work-ba0ed9fd-questions 41dd6eae (2026-10-28) with 'The video recording is invalid or exceeds 10 MiB.' after 12.4 s, while the gate built several crates in parallel; three reruns alone passed in about 2.3 s each. R7 does not touch client/media. Find which check finish() failed under load (too few frames, a short duration or a missing moov) and make the recorder or the test robust to a slow encoder.
notes: Root cause (verified 2026-10-28): the Linux recorder's preview and poster appsinks keep one frame (max-buffers=1 drop=true) that nobody pulls once stopping starts, and appsink's wait-on-eos property (default true since GStreamer 1.8) blocks the EOS until that buffer is consumed. Whenever a frame was queued at that moment, the pipeline never posted EOS and the recording was refused as invalid after the finish wait. Fix: wait-on-eos=false on both appsinks (0eaeb07f); the mux branch has no appsink, so EOS still waits for the real file. Evidence: 2 of 25 standalone runs hung before, 0 of 80 after; arch gate 982 passed. Defence in depth kept: a 30 s finish wait (FINISH_TIMEOUT, Cancel checked every 100 ms on Linux and macOS) and a stderr line naming the check behind every refusal (0e8107a3, 76b26bef). macOS and Windows use no appsink.

title: Tauri client: a project catalog on computers without the Qt GUI (swarm initialize without a GUI cache)
description:
Follow-up of the organization plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-28-tauri-client-organization.md, deviation 3 in its Decisions), filed by its Task 10 on 2026-10-28.

The Tauri client never runs `hgs swarm initialize`. An initialize from it would mark the catalog imported and skip the Qt GUI's one-time import of its local organization (src/swarm/mod.rs:212-215, SwarmController.cpp:86-88). So on a computer where the Qt GUI never ran, `swarm get` reports `initialized: false` and every project edit stays disabled with "Project sync is not set up on this computer yet. Start Zerus here once to import its projects."

Decide how such a computer gets a catalog:
- an initialize from the client with an empty organization (or the name-derived projects) when no Qt organization exists, or an hgs-side initialize that needs no GUI cache;
- what the Qt GUI's first start does afterwards with its own local organization (import, merge or review);
- whether the client may initialize at all is an owner decision.

Keep the rule that this client sends intent only: placement and concurrent heads stay in hgs and the replica.
notes:
Owner initialization ruling requested through design-ac; acknowledged under wait c16996c1. Current hgs initialize consumes the single imported marker, which would suppress a later Qt cache import. Recommendation sent: CLI-side empty catalog bootstrap with a separate later GUI import marker. Initialization semantics remain unchanged pending the owner answer.
Owner ruling via design-ac, 2026-10-29: when no Qt organization cache exists, hgs bootstraps an empty name-free catalog; client sends intent only and placement/concurrent heads stay in hgs/replica. A separate explicit import marker preserves a later Qt first-start local-organization import. Computers with an existing Qt cache keep the current path. Keep peers and old CLI callers compatible, preserving swarm get/initialize semantics for existing callers; document in docs/reference.md. Approved as the result of wait c16996c1.
Queued behind the new owner bar order: A2-4/A2-2 findings, A2-3, A2-5, archived composer, exit handshake. No bootstrap source changes yet. Webui approved conservative Qt settings-store presence (including unknown/error types), a separate node-bound pending GUI import marker with imported=true for old callers, marker-before-bootstrap save and save-before-marker-clear ordering, and triggers on swarm get plus initial organization watch subscription. Steady-state reads remain lock-free.

A separate explicit import marker keeps the Qt GUI's later first-start import of its local organization possible. Computers with a Qt cache keep today's path. Existing swarm get/initialize callers stay compatible. Implementer: a2hub.

title: Tauri client: follow session renames made while the client was closed (Qt's persisted run tokens, SessionOrganization.cpp:223-245)
description:
Follow-up of the organization plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-28-tauri-client-organization.md, deviation 5 in its Decisions), filed by its Task 10 on 2026-10-28.

Qt keeps `runs` (`<machine>\n<run>` to the session identity) and `run_groups` in its local organization (SessionOrganization.cpp:59 and toJson 336). On start, `observe` (SessionOrganization.cpp:223-245) finds a known run under a new name and calls `renameSession`, so a session renamed while Qt was closed keeps its explicit project.

The Tauri client migrates only the renames it observes while it runs (the grouping's renames, `Intent::Renamed`, one apply when the old name was explicit). Its layout file (`organization-layout.json`, `client/core/src/swarm/layout.rs`) keeps no run tokens, so a session renamed while the client was closed falls back to the default project until someone moves it, unless the Qt GUI migrated it first.

Scope:
- persist each member's run token in the layout, bounded like the member order (at most 100,000 members);
- on the first presented catalog, migrate a known run under a new name through the same `Intent::Renamed` path: one apply, only when the old name was explicit, and nothing when the other writer already migrated it (the two-writer tests in `client/core/tests/swarm_sync.rs`);
- keep Qt's archive exclusions; archived identities are zerus-5wmh.17.
notes:
Implementation paused for binding A2-4 review fixes. Local regressions pass for persisted rename discovery before/after row arrival, one apply, another writer already migrated, independent runs-file debounce, bounded exit with stuck token I/O, and failed-save replacement. webui rulings: separate organization-runs.json (replay variant), newest 100000 writes oldest-first eviction; background startup load; independent RunsWriter lock; exit waits at most 500 ms then draft/layout flush continues. Full gates and publication remain.
Published work-6768c5c5-rename-tokens at cc90e197; sent to webui for independent review. Arch 16/16: core 888, src-tauri 469 twice, vitest 1300, Windows clippy both crates. Mac 11/11: core 887, src-tauri 461 twice, vitest 1300. Fifteen authored tests executed; fourteen guard mutants caught/restored. Privacy and pinned gitleaks passed. Evidence SHA256SUMS 1603f4bd32d84018f8b2a352b5e4f0026e9659f5e6836761c27b1dc6b9727ce2. Core received the published dependency head for archive grouping. Review remains pending.
Webui recheck requests changes on cc90e197: retain old persisted token until Renamed is consumed (two-start not-ready/exit probe); debounce/rank/runs.rename regressions; preserve history on read errors and prove full-cap bytes; move serialization and I/O to an independent writer thread from a cheap snapshot; deadline-based exit tests; explicit replay flag. Branch not ready to fold. Fixes follow A2 bar items per coordinator. Core informed that .40 dependency is unsettled.

title: Tauri client: attention and working counts follow Qt's online rule (unread keeps counting offline)
description:
Qt parity for counts while a computer is offline. Found in the organization Task 7 review on 2026-10-28.

Qt's rules:
- Attention counts only while the computer is online, except review-later (SessionsWindowRows.cpp:400-401).
- Working counts only while the computer is online (currentActivity, SessionPresentation.h:263-271).
- Unread replies of an offline computer do count, through visibleUnreadReply(online) = unreadReply && (!online || !replyInProgress()), in HgsClient.h:104-105. Do not exclude them.

The webview counts attention and working from last-known statuses, so a project header can say "2 working" while its cards say Offline.

Apply Qt's online rule consistently, backed by computerOffline:
- the project header counts: pass offline(computer) into ListInput and apply it to attention and working only;
- counts() in store/ui.ts;
- the state filters (matchesFilter).

Unread follows visibleUnreadReply. It is not a regression: the base code counted the same way.
notes:

title: Tauri client: renderer policy for NVIDIA Wayland (ZERUS_CLIENT_RENDERER)
description: From spike zerus-5wmh.29. Before GTK, WebKit or any thread starts, the client decides its renderer: ZERUS_CLIENT_RENDERER=auto|dmabuf|shm plus a client setting applied after restart. auto: if WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER is unset, on NVIDIA proprietary + Wayland (detect /proc/driver/nvidia/version, the desktop DRM card's driver, nvidia_drm modeset Y; Wayland as GDK decides: GDK_BACKEND unset or wayland and a Wayland socket) add __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1; if the variable is set to anything but 0, respect it and say so once in diagnostics. dmabuf: WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=0 plus the explicit-sync variable on NVIDIA Wayland, guarded by a crash marker (written before GTK starts with renderer and driver version, cleared on the page's first frame after load; a marker present at start uses shared memory once and logs why; a driver change retries once). shm: always shared memory. Never touch system configuration. Blocked on the owner's answer about why /etc/environment sets the variable (relayed by the coordinator): if it is only for Error 71 crashes, auto may also override with the marker. Also handle the GL path painting while minimised (pause motion on focus loss or WebKit visibility).
close_reason: Duplicate of zerus-5wmh.37 (the coordinator's filing of the same renderer policy; no settings control, the environment variable is the switch).

title: Tauri client on Linux: choose the WebKit renderer per process (spike .29 option a)
description: Coordinator 2026-10-28, from the zerus-5wmh.29 report (Client-side renderer policy). On NVIDIA Wayland the shared-memory renderer repaints the whole window every frame (about 4.3-5 ms app CPU per frame, CPU linear in frame rate: client tree 76.7-80.6% incl. KWin at 60 fps), while DMA-BUF with __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1 measured 17.7-20.5% with the UI verified non-blank by GTK back-buffer readback; DMA-BUF without that variable dies at start with Wayland Error 71 (6/6). Implement option (a): at the top of main(), before Tauri/GTK/threads, apply ZERUS_CLIENT_RENDERER=auto|dmabuf|shm (default auto). auto with WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER absent: on NVIDIA Wayland (proc driver version, the desktop DRM card on nvidia, nvidia_drm modeset Y; Wayland decided as GDK does) add __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1, else change nothing. auto with the variable set to anything but 0: respect it, stay on shared memory, and report it once in diagnostics. dmabuf: WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=0 plus the NVIDIA variable on NVIDIA Wayland, guarded by a crash marker written before GTK starts (renderer, driver version, time), cleared on the first rAF after load; a marker found at start falls back to shared memory for that start and logs why; keyed to the driver version so an update retries once. shm: WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1. XWayland (GDK_BACKEND=x11): leave as is. Known gap to track separately: on the GL path a minimised window keeps painting (18.5-21.9%) because a Wayland client cannot learn it was minimised. A settings control is out of scope unless the owner asks; the environment variable is the switch.
close_reason: Renderer policy merged as 6fd7231f (#413): ZERUS_CLIENT_RENDERER=auto|dmabuf|shm, crash marker cleared after the first frame; real-display check on arch NVIDIA Wayland posted on the PR.

title: Tauri client: Activity and session-list scrolling miss frames at high refresh rates
description: Coordinator 2026-10-28. The real client on the owner's 144 Hz KDE display with Kimi's patched WebKitGTK/GTK stack (zerus-5wmh.28; evidence arch-client-full-144.json in the webkit-vblank workspace) paces rAF and transform animations at 144 Hz (mean 6.95 ms, p95 7), but scrolling cannot keep up: list-scroll mean 8.01 ms, median 7, p95 14, max 23; activity-scroll mean 11.59 ms, median 9, p95 27, max 98 (43% of frames over 1.5 frame periods). left-animation mean 7.19, p95 10. At the stock 60 Hz every scenario sits at 16 ms, so the limit was hidden. The Mac 120 Hz run (client/bench/results/mac-client-2026-10-28.json) skipped activity-scroll with 'nothing to scroll', so the Mac has no Activity measurement at all. title: Tauri client core T1b: Windows ConPTY for the Terminal attach
description: Port tray/src/PtyProcess_win.cpp into client/core behind terminal::Attach (T1 ships the Unix port). The attach client must start suspended inside a kill-on-close job object before it resumes, so a stop or a client crash ends hgs.exe and its ssh.exe. Stop closes the pseudoconsole first (CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT, off the UI thread because ClosePseudoConsole may wait for the output to drain), waits for the graceful stop, then terminates the job; it waits at most 2 s. Keep reads bounded at 256 KiB per chunk, the 4 MiB input bound, ResizePseudoConsole with T1's clamps, Windows command-line quoting and a sorted environment block. portable-pty 0.9 starts processes neither suspended nor in a job, so use windows-sys directly. Needs a Windows CI or test run before merge; the events session may not use the Windows dev PC.
