title: Spike: why WebKitGTK spends about 20% of a core per idle animation frame in the app process
description: Coordinator 2026-10-28 (option B): on the real arch display the client built from main idles at 33.6% CPU with six CSS animations running (app 19.9%, web 9.5%) against 4.7% with them off; the Mac idles at about 3%. Find where the app-process cost goes and whether it can be cut without changing the approved motion: DMA-BUF versus shared-memory renderer (WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER), the compositing mode (WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE), XWayland, GTK GL, a profile of the app process, and stepped pulses (fewer distinct frames). Nothing changes for the owner until there are results.
notes:
Spike result 2026-10-28 (arch KDE Wayland, NVIDIA 615.78.08, 144 Hz): the app-process idle cost is the shared-memory renderer, forced desktop-wide by WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 in the owner's /etc/environment. GTK repaints the whole 1440x900 window per frame (4.3-5.1 ms app CPU per frame, about two thirds kernel page faults on fresh Wayland shm buffers, plus about 4 ms in KWin), so app CPU scales with the frame rate (27-32% at 62 fps, 54% at 136 fps). None of it is in the client's Rust or TypeScript. DMA-BUF alone dies at start with Wayland Error 71 (6 of 6); DMA-BUF with __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1 for the client process: total 17.7% and 20.5% (app 5.5/6.5%) against 76.7-80.6% (app 29-32%) on shared memory, two 5-minute runs. CSS-only changes do not keep the approved motion (steps(4) cuts the app to 3.3% but steps the pulse; will-change no effect); XWayland moves the cost elsewhere. The first idle window is the steady motion cost, not settling or GC; the low after-minimise window was the window still minimised. Recommendation: renderer policy option (a) refined (ZERUS_CLIENT_RENDERER=auto|dmabuf|shm, respect an explicit global =1 by default, add only the explicit-sync variable when unset, dmabuf behind a crash marker keyed to the driver version), pending the owner's answer on why the variable is set. Open: web process cost with Activity pulses; GL path paints at 60 rather than 144.
Evidence (sha256 prefixes of client.log / samples.jsonl / report.json per run, 'as displayed' window, total/app/web/kwin %): base-c SHM 76.7/31.7/34.9/32.3 def82ed29576/047f84677c1a/5111adff8f96; base-d SHM 80.6/28.9/41.8/32.1 6b72f0426370/8558fe472d01/f60cfa8d41d2; on-nvsync DMA-BUF+explicit-sync 17.7/5.5/5.5/9.9 34308165f818/4a7b1355d3cf/59722a913573; on-nvsync-b 20.5/6.5/4.8/7.2 1d68bbd581ea/969dfbe27c0e/4c0370da022b; base-shim SHM pre-restart 47.6/26.9/13.3 3ae301e13693/f7dbc2b1b939/e2644520715b; dmabuf-on (DMA-BUF alone) died at start, client.log a8e1ec1eb4d2. Reduce motion about 8-11% total on both paths; hidden about 9%. Policy: option (a) refined, accepted by the coordinator as zerus-5wmh.37 (respect an explicit global WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER; when unset on NVIDIA proprietary + Wayland add __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1; ZERUS_CLIENT_RENDERER=dmabuf opts in behind a crash marker keyed to the driver version; shm forces shared memory; variables set at the top of main() before any thread; Wayland decided as GDK does, not by XDG_SESSION_TYPE). Blank-output detection (option b) unproven: a GTK back-buffer glReadPixels showed the UI colours, but no failing case was available. Known follow-ups: zerus-5wmh.39 (GL path paints while minimised); open questions: web-process cost with Activity pulses, GL path painting at 60 rather than 144. The full report is committed with zerus-5wmh.37's branch as client/bench/results/spike-29-webkitgtk-idle-2026-10-28.md.
close_reason: Answered: the idle cost is WebKitGTK's shared-memory renderer forced by the global environment; fix is zerus-5wmh.37's per-process renderer policy (17.7-20.5% total against 76.7-80.6%). Findings and evidence hashes in the notes.

title: Tauri client core: hgs reads for the phase 3 screens
description: A reads module in client/core for Overview, Projects, Machines, Accounts and Settings: hgs [@host] <command> --json off the UI thread through run::run (lands with phase 2, zerus-5wmh.7; reuse its bounded output and timeouts, do not duplicate), typed decoding, fixtures and tests. First step, startable now: an inventory of the reads the Qt screens use (command, JSON shape, refresh trigger), recorded in this bead's notes for the phase 3 plan. Code starts after phase 2 merges.
notes:
Step 1 inventory (2026-10-28, events session): hgs reads behind the Qt Overview, Projects, Machines, Accounts and Settings screens. Sources: tray/src/{DashboardPage,ProjectsDialog,SwarmController,MachinesPage,AccountsPage,AnalyticsClient}.cpp and HgsClient.cpp. Shapes are the top-level keys from the installed CLI.

OVERVIEW (DashboardPage): reads nothing of its own. Data comes from the fleet: the watch catalog plus catalog.meta per computer. Machine tiles use catalog.meta.metrics: cpu_percent, cpu_count, cpu_state, cpu_interval_seconds, memory_used_bytes, memory_total_bytes, platform, sampled_at. Session tiles use catalog rows. Accounts summary uses the Accounts data below. Re-render: on every fleet change, every 15 s while visible (ages), and elapsed labels every 1 s. => The client needs no new read for Overview beyond the stream plus the Accounts read.

PROJECTS (ProjectsDialog + SwarmController):
- `hgs [@host] project ls --json` returns a JSON array of projects (empty array when there are none). It's called per host when the dialog opens or a host is chosen.
- `hgs swarm get` returns the organization: {conflicts, digest, initialized, machines[{connection,id,local,name}], node_id, organization, peers, preferences, schema, swarm_id, versions, worker, written}. SwarmController polls it every 5 s (the source of the 4-6 swarm get per minute), timeout 10 s.
- Writes, which belong to phase 2 actions: `swarm apply` with stdin {base, desired, versions}, `swarm preview|sync|join|bind|resolve` (network, 180 s timeout).

MACHINES (MachinesPage):
- `hgs machine` (ls) returns {environment_override, local, machines[{alias, connection, enabled, inherited, source}], revision}; timeout 8 s. Called on show and after every mutation (reload skips while a request runs, an install runs, or the editor is dirty).
- `hgs machine resolve <alias>` resolves the selected connection.
- `hgs machine check <alias>` is a connectivity check, timeout 25 s.
- Writes: `machine <op> <target> --revision R` (add/edit/remove).
- `hgs session-host status|install --json` (Windows local host): status 15 s, install 60 s.

ACCOUNTS (AccountsPage):
- `hgs [@host] account ls` returns {defaults, host, profiles[], removed_profiles[], revision}. profile keys include id, label, native, installed, is_default, auth_status, auth_revision, account_status, credential_file, home, effective_permission_mode, permission_detail, model_defaults(_supported), and more. Timeout 25 s. Called on show (ensureCatalogs), every 30 s while visible, and after mutations ("copy" forces it).
- Background `hgs [@host] account inspect <id>` for usage: one at a time per account, the profile inspection behind the usage meters.
- Writes take `--revision <catalog revision>`: account add/set-key (90 s)/copy (60 s)/start (60 s).

SETTINGS (pages reached from Settings):
- `hgs --version`, timeout 3 s.
- Analytics: `hgs [@host] analytics --json` with stdin {schema:1, action:"summary", from, through} returns {buckets, collection, coverage, generated_at, machine_id, range, revision, schema, source, source_epoch}. Gated by the help marker "hgs [@host] analytics --json". Writes: configure/purge with expected_epoch.
- Speech stats: `hgs [@host] speech --json` with stdin {action:"stats", ...}, gated by its marker.
- Mobile devices: `hgs [@host] mobile ...`, help-gated (an older CLI would launch an agent).
- Recovery: `hgs [@host] recovery get` (also polled, 2-7 per minute).

title: hgs watch: one watcher per computer for all local and remote clients
description: Measured 2026-10-28 on arch (Dev 1456): each hgs watch --json spends ~4% of a core itself and ~13-14% in short-lived children, mostly tmux capture-pane for the 5 s whole listing (owner chose 5 s). arch runs two (its own GUI's and the one serving the Mac over SSH), and every further client (web client, connector) adds another. Share one watcher per computer (a local fan-out the CLI stream attaches to), or reuse one listing pass across streams, keeping watch-v1 unchanged. Evidence: events-data-plane review page section 0, raw/arch-watch-split-1456.txt and raw/arch-watch-for-mac-1456.txt.
notes: 2026-10-28 measured split: per check git-status runs ~4.6-5.6 git processes; the GUI watcher's children were dominated by git checks that both arch watchers duplicated. Chosen fix (cheaper than one shared watcher process, watch-v1 unchanged): streams of one computer share git checks through private kept-check files in the state directory, gated by change time and Git metadata stat, with a per-folder lock so concurrent needs run Git once. A/B on arch, two isolated watchers, 20 real folders: safety ticks only 649 -> 347 checks, children CPU 34.3 -> 18.6 s; with 225 synthetic Bash calls in 180 s 1348 -> 615 checks, 5660 -> 2778 git processes, children CPU 93.0 -> 48.4 s; identical final states. PR #387. Listing-side children (rev-parse --show-toplevel and symbolic-ref per pane per re-list, tmux capture-pane) are unchanged and remain a possible follow-up.
close_reason: Merged in #387 (3ad508b9): watch streams of one computer share git checks; A/B 1348 -> 615 checks, child CPU 93 -> 48 s with identical states. Re-measure after the next Dev install.

title: Tauri client: WebKitGTK paces at 60 Hz on the 144 Hz KDE Wayland desktop
description: Measured 2026-10-28 on the owner's arch desktop (KDE Plasma Wayland, two 144 Hz outputs at scale 1, NVIDIA RTX 3090 Ti with nvidia-drm modeset plus an AMD Raphael iGPU, WebKitGTK 2.54.1 through webkit2gtk-4.1): requestAnimationFrame, CSS transform and left animations and list scrolling all run at 16.06 ms intervals instead of 6.94 ms, both in client/bench/harness (cross-origin isolated, 0.02 ms timer) and in the dev client. Find why WebKitGTK paces at 60 Hz here (its display refresh or vblank monitor on NVIDIA and Wayland, the output the window is on, GDK frame clock), whether a supported setting or a newer WebKitGTK paces at the display rate, and check an AMD iGPU output if one is connected. If WebKitGTK cannot pace at the display rate on this hardware, evaluate the CEF runtime per the spec's Linux fallback with the same harness. Results feed zerus-5wmh.4.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text: Source analysis 2026-10-28 (WebKitGTK 2.54.1 tarball, read-only device checks; real-display confirmation pending): WebKitGTK falls back to its 60 Hz timer (DisplayVBlankMonitorTimer.cpp:40-49, 16 ms sleeps, matches the measured 16.06 ms) because DisplayVBlankMonitorDRM::findCrtc only accepts a connector whose mm size equals gdk_monitor_get_width_mm/height_mm, and KWin reports 597x336 and 797x334 mm while the kernel connectors report 600x340 and 800x330 mm. Even with a match, nvidia-drm runs with vblank=N (default) and drmWaitVBlank returns EOPNOTSUPP on all CRTCs; and PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPS is on by default for GTK too, which would cap 144 Hz at 72 Hz unless disabled per web view. No environment variable selects the DRM monitor or raises the timer. The AMD iGPU has no driver bound and drives no output. Reaching 144 Hz needs nvidia_drm vblank support (kernel option, owner's call), a size-tolerant connector match in WebKit (or the experiment's shim), and the near-60 feature off in the client. Tools: client/bench/webkitgtk-drm-probe.py, webkitgtk-monitor-mm-shim.c, webkitgtk-vblank-experiments.sh (branch of the investigation agent, to land in the follow-up PR). The real-display experiment is armed to run at the next unlock.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text: Window-less probe (client/bench/webkitgtk-drm-probe.py --compositor), run by the coordinator 2026-10-28 06:2x UTC with the KDE session unlocked and both outputs on: connector routing is fine (DP-2 encoder_id 836 on CRTC index 0, ACTIVE 1; DP-3 encoder_id 840 on CRTC index 1, ACTIVE 1; both 144 Hz), which settles the unknown routing row. The size match still fails (KWin DP-2 597x336 mm vs kernel 600x340; DP-3 797x334 vs 800x330). drmWaitVBlank answers Operation not supported on all four CRTCs. /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/vblank reads N and is read-only (0444), so enabling it needs a module reload, in practice a reboot. Expectation: the size shim alone still falls back to the timer.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text: Real-display experiment 2026-10-28 06:03:45-06:05:02 UTC (session unlocked, both outputs on, 144 Hz; harness window, WebKitGTK 2.54.1). Every native Wayland configuration paces the CSS transform animation at the 60 Hz timer (mean 16.06 ms): default, WEBKIT_DEBUG=DisplayLink, near-60 feature off, the GDK monitor mm shim (797x334->800x330, 597x336->600x340), shim plus near-60 off, and the forced timer. Without the shim WebKit logs 'Could not create a vblank monitor for display 2: no drm node with CRTC found' (DisplayVBlankMonitorDRM.cpp:226). With the shim it passes the size match and finds the CRTC, then fails at 'drmWaitVBlank failed: Operation not permitted' (DisplayVBlankMonitorDRM.cpp:238) and falls back to the timer. So the size match is the first blocker and nvidia-drm's missing vblank (vblank=N) the second; 144 Hz needs both fixed. XWayland paces at 60 Hz through vblank (16.67 ms). rAF on a light page averages 6.94 ms with a median of 4-6 ms in every native configuration: irregular callbacks, not display pacing.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text: EDID cause (coordinator, 2026-10-28, from card1-DP-* EDID, sizes only): both sizes are legitimate EDID fields. The kernel connector size is the base block's whole-centimetre field times 10 (DP-2 60x34 cm -> 600x340 mm, DP-3 80x33 cm -> 800x330 mm); KWin reports the detailed timing descriptor's millimetre image size (DP-2 597x336, DP-3 797x334). Not a KWin bug: the fragile part is WebKit's exact equality between two EDID fields. A robust upstream fix matches by connector name (wl_output v4 name such as DP-2 equals the DRM connector name) or compares with a tolerance.

comments.author: ufna

title: Measure Tauri vs tuned Qt on one heavy screen; macOS must pace at the display rate
description:
Two-week spike after design approval: session list plus long Activity on the
watch-v1 data plane. Metrics: p95 scroll frame time, input-to-frame latency,
session open time, idle CPU, RSS, batched Channel throughput, 20k-50k list,
xterm.js WebGL vs DOM, KDE fractional scales, NVIDIA. Decide WebKitGTK vs
CEF (Tauri 3) vs Electron for Linux by numbers.

Hard pass/fail (owner requirement, 2026-10-27): on macOS, frame pacing equals
the display refresh rate (120 Hz on ProMotion) for scrolling, CSS animations
and requestAnimationFrame. Primary route: Tauri 2 WKWebView with the WebKit
preference PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled disabled through
WKPreferences _features/_setEnabled:forFeature: before webview creation
(with_webview_configuration, Tauri 2.8+). Criteria on the owner's ProMotion Mac
(AC power, Low Power Mode off, 3 x 10 s runs, worst counts, T = 8.33 ms):
(1) rAF light page and during a transform animation: mean T +/- 1%, median
T +/- 0.5 ms, >= 99% of intervals <= 1.5 T, <= 0.2% > 2.5 T, < 1% in 15-18.5 ms;
(2) window capture >= 117.6 changed frames/s for a transform animation, a
non-accelerated animation and virtual-list scrolling; (3) validity: a native
display-link control reads >= 117.6 Hz and a run with the preference at its
default must fail (1). Power reported, not gated. If WKWebView fails or the SPI
disappears, run the same harness on Chromium for macOS (Tauri 3 CEF once beta,
otherwise Electron) and bring the trade-off to the owner. Details: the web UI
design spec, "Risks and measurement plan".

If it fails or the preference disappears, evaluate Chromium on macOS (Tauri 3 CEF once beta, otherwise Electron) with the same harness. Recorded in the web UI spec.

acceptance_criteria: Classify fixture versus product from concrete retained evidence. A fixture fix needs deterministic original-red/fixed controls showing readiness for the exact config/render generation rather than an old screen, without increasing timeouts, blind signal/input retries or weakening assertions. notes:
2026-10-18 diagnosis (agent-question): failure is in configure() before any hgs call; the pane stayed alive (capture-pane never failed). The module took 49.7 s against 33.5-36.7 s when passing, which fits all 100 polls running out with the footer absent. Candidate mechanism: configure(panel=False) returns on an already-absent footer, so the next configure signals while render #1 may be in progress. CPython nests signal handlers (probe: the inner one finishes first), so the older screen is written last. Latent siblings: non-atomic config write; hgs answer returns on transcript evidence before the fake rewrites config and redraws. Product not implicated. Proposed test-only hunk (atomic config, generation barrier, latest-wins redraw, single config writer, bounded diagnostics) sent to root; holding for GO before any edit, build or fixture run.
2026-10-18 root review of the first proposal (d0d2) was CHANGES_REQUIRED, with three findings: lost wakeup at the redraw handoff, handle() not snapshotting its config, and the rendered file proving only the PTY write. Revised design: the SIGUSR1 handler is a no-op that only feeds the wakeup pipe; the fake's main loop drains the pipe and then redraws, handling pending input first; handle() uses one config snapshot; each screen ends with an OSC 2 generation title and configure waits for that pane title within the unchanged wait budget. Revised test-only diff and a deterministic gate-based control plan (C1, C1b, H, S, C2, optional T) sent; holding for GO.
2026-10-18 test-only source result c25f464e (base 5310eb5e, local branch fix/pvfa-codex-question-fixture, not pushed) is the reviewed revised diff, applied exactly. Built hgs once. Controls ran once per arm with forced gate interleavings: C1, C1b, H and S gave RED on the counterexample arm and GREEN on FIXED. title: Decide device/workspace enrollment, membership and service quotas
description: Audit 2026-10-18: by design the relay has no signup, workspace creation or administrator HTTP endpoint; provisioning is a local CLI. It limits each credential to 2,400 requests a minute and has workspace queue and payload budgets, but no per-plan quotas or billing. Owner product decision needed before implementation.
design: Final approved device/workspace model is specified in docs/encrypted-workspaces.md. An unconfigured computer explicitly creates a workspace or joins using a computer-specific code from an active trusted computer; phones use separate purpose-bound invitations. Each endpoint generates independent random credentials/signing/encryption keys locally and persists its exact candidate before HTTP. The relay receives public proofs and signed membership, never invitation secrets or private keys; current trusted computers verify and approve candidates. A workspace contains independently enrolled gateways and their direct SSH routes. Change workspace confirms consequences, drains/journals existing native work, preserves old receipts, retires a protected gateway by exact signed change and activates a new identity/private journal only after durable target admission. Legacy unconfirmed retirement permits only a separate explicit local-disconnect confirmation; protected retirement has no such fallback. No user account/password recovery is introduced; lost state uses a fresh trusted-device invitation or a new workspace. Operator-only standard/team policy reserves bounded capacity inside declared request/poll/DB/body/spool/push/storage totals; public clients cannot self-promote. Billing and operational launch remain with the managed-service epic.
acceptance_criteria: An approved product decision for account authentication, workspace membership and plan quotas that keeps the self-hosted CLI provisioning path.

title: P4 Kimi native answer channel spike and unviewed growth
description: Spike whether the Kimi wire protocol observed for kimi_wire questions can carry answers without terminal keys. Also add layer A (question_terminal::fit_unviewed) for Kimi question dialogs: deferred from zerus-0yrj task 3 because no Kimi question native harness exists; build one with an isolated Kimi and localhost API first. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-native-answer-channels-design.md.
notes:
Finding 2026-10-18 (Kimi 2.1.1 bundled hook handling): hook output is read only for hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision == deny (plus message); no allow, updatedInput or answers path exists. So Kimi hooks cannot carry question answers or approvals; Kimi questions stay on screen delivery and need layer A growth, which first needs an isolated Kimi question native harness.
Finding 2026-10-18 (Kimi 2.1.1 bundle source): the interactive TUI bootstraps the agent engine in its own process (node-sdk SDKRpcClientV2 -> bootstrap). Questions and approvals reach TUI controllers through in-memory reverse RPC (src/tui/reverse-rpc/question, approval) and resolve only via the panel. The local server API (/api/v1/sessions/{id}/questions/{tail}, kap-server) exists only in a separate kimi web/rc process with its own interaction registry, and would resume the session as a second owner; the TUI never starts it. The session notify/state.json is an enabled flag, not an inbox; wire.jsonl is output only; hooks are deny-only. So no native answer channel exists for a running Kimi TUI: questions, plan review and approvals stay on verified screen delivery plus layer A growth.
Hazard 2026-10-18: a native Kimi spike that ran the shared ~/.kimi-code/bin executable let Kimi's background auto-install (tui.toml [upgrade] auto_install defaults true) replace that executable with 2.2.0. Native Kimi tests must run a private copy of a pinned binary and set KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1.
Source result 2026-10-18 on branch work/kimi-unviewed (200fe270, beb9474d, d22e204e, 49779fd7; base dfe25722): no native answer channel in Kimi 2.1.1 (engine in the TUI process); layer A for clipped Kimi question dialogs. Native NativeKimiQuestions on sealed private copies of 2.1.1 and 2.2.0: base red 'the native question dialog is not visible; open Terminal' on both, fixed 3/3 on both. Awaiting root acceptance.

title: P4 Codex native answer channel spike
description: Spike, like the Claude PermissionRequest spike for zerus-0yrj: can Codex hooks or its app-server answer codex_async questions and approvals while the TUI runs, without terminal keys? Pinned Codex versions, isolated home and tmux socket. Outcome: a channel adapter (bind, available, deliver, confirm, close) plugged into questions.rs routing, or a documented no. notes:
Also from zerus-0yrj task 3 (deferred): check natively whether codex_async question panels can be clipped in an unviewed 80x24 pane; if so add clipped/complete detectors and question_terminal::fit_unviewed for them.
Finding 2026-10-18 (Codex 0.162.1 binary hook schema): PermissionRequestDecisionWire has behavior allow|deny and message; updatedInput, updatedPermissions and interrupt=true are reserved and make PermissionRequest hooks fail closed. So Codex hooks cannot carry question answers: codex_async questions keep screen delivery with layer A; a Codex approval channel (allow/deny with message) is possible and needs a native spike. Codex app-server is not attached to the interactive TUI.
Spike result 2026-10-18 (private pinned Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0 images, byte-identical to their SHA-512-verified tarballs, plus a private copy of 0.162.1; isolated CODEX_HOME, --no-daemon, update check off, localhost Responses fixture, isolated tmux): no Codex channel. A synchronous PermissionRequest hook runs before the approval panel, which appears only after the hook returns without a decision ('Running hook' meanwhile); its allow runs the command and its deny with a message shows 'Blocked by hook'. With async: true the panel shows at once but the hook decision is ignored. No Kind, protocol or registration change. Clipping confirmed: an open codex_async panel taller than its pane keeps the title and scrolls its answers, naming the visible row in the key hints ('option 1/6'); hgs then reported the composer reason and Submit stayed unavailable. title: Answer Claude tool approvals through the PermissionRequest answer channel
description:
Phase P3 of the native answer channel design (zerus-0yrj, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-native-answer-channels-design.md, C for Claude approvals). Answer claude_tool_approval cards through the shared PermissionRequest channel instead of TUI keys, keeping A (question_terminal::fit_unviewed, zerus-6uhz) as the fallback.

Spike 2026-10-17, real Claude 2.1.296, localhost API, isolated tmux, private HOME:
- allow: decision {behavior: allow} without updatedPermissions runs the tool once with no panel; settings and settings.local.json stay unchanged.
- deny with message, no interrupt: the model receives the message as an is_error tool_result and the turn continues (maps to No with feedback).
- deny with interrupt: true: identical to the TUI No: 'Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?', no tool_result, no Stop hook. Use it for No.
- Dangerous-rm safety confirmation of the main agent in bypassPermissions mode does emit PermissionRequest; the panel shows while the hook waits and a hook allow removes it and runs the command. Hook-less claude_terminal_safety stays on A/Terminal.
- PermissionRequest fields: cwd, effort, hook_event_name, permission_mode, permission_suggestions, prompt_id, session_id, tool_input, tool_name, transcript_path (agent_id for children). No tool_use_id; prompt_id is per user prompt and is shared by concurrent requests, so it is not an identity.
- Two Bash calls in one message are serialized: PreToolUse 2 follows PostToolUse 1, so one Bash request waits at a time. Two Read calls outside the working directory produce two simultaneous PermissionRequests (TUI shows 1 of 2); each hook process's decision reaches its own tool_use_id. Bind each request to the active PreToolUse with exactly equal tool_name and tool_input; equal inputs pending together stay ambiguous (screen).
- Terminal answer first: Claude neither kills nor signals the waiting hook; a later deny is ignored and the tool still runs. The channel must exit on the bound PostToolUse/tool_result.
- Hook timeout: Claude sends SIGTERM at the hook's timeout and the panel stays (fallback to A).
- A silent PermissionRequest hook (the existing journal entry) beside a deciding one does not prevent the decision.

title: Host backend parity for growing unviewed panes that clip native panels
description: TerminalBackend::grow_unviewed (zerus-6uhz) lets question listings grow a pane no client views, doubling its height up to question_terminal::MAX_UNVIEWED_ROWS until a clipped native panel fits. title: Mark agent-originated hgs send with a compact sender envelope
description: Receiving tier of the parent epic: a recipient must recognize a message written by another agent and know how to reply.
design:
For agent-originated `hgs send` (source already proven by send_origin), wrap the delivered text in one compact envelope with the sender's session name, machine and zerus:// reference. Owner, desktop, Android, iOS and connector sends stay unchanged. The receipt and idempotency hash cover the exact delivered text. Desktop, Android and iOS Activity show it as a peer message with the sender, not as the person's message (extend journal::system_prompt classification and shared fixtures).

This changes visible message content across clients: confirm the envelope format with the owner before shipping.
acceptance_criteria:
- Recipient can run `hgs inspect` on the envelope reference and reply without other context.
- Non-agent sends are byte-identical to today.
- Desktop/Android/iOS render the peer message consistently from shared fixtures.
- Owner approval of the envelope format recorded in this bead.

title: Deliver the static hgs hint to every agent start without accumulation
description: Always-on tier of the parent epic: one byte-stable sentence pointing at hgs guide, delivered through a native channel per provider and kept correct across the lifecycle matrix in the epic.
design:
Deliver the static one-sentence hint (see the parent epic) to every agent hgs starts, through the per-provider channel described in the epic:
- DeepSeek Harness and OpenCode: hgs-owned instructions.
- Claude Code, Codex and Kimi: SessionStart hook additional context on startup/clear/compact, and on resume only without a per-conversation delivery mark. Store the mark in the binding as {conversation_id, hint revision}.
- Otherwise a launch-time flag merged with user values, re-added at each launch and resume and kept out of saved base argv (statusline pattern in src/state/lifecycle.rs).

First verify for each pinned native version whether hook context persists across native resume and is re-requested after compaction. Choose the mechanism from that evidence, not assumption. Hook-added context must not appear as a person's message in Activity.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests for every lifecycle path in the epic matrix, including repeated resume without duplication and pre-feature conversations receiving the hint on first resume.
- User --append-system-prompt / developer instructions, --system-prompt, --settings and project launchers keep working; saved base argv unchanged.
- Opt-out (global and per account) suppresses injection.
- Native contract coverage on the pinned Claude Code and Codex matrices proves the delivery mechanism; a skipped suite is not evidence.
notes:
Source 87b0b7d5 on branch feat/agent-coordination-hint (base main dfe25722), not delivered. Native evidence on private SHA-512 pinned copies, keyless fixture, isolated homes: Claude 2.1.296 and Codex 0.160.1/0.162.0 keep SessionStart additionalContext in the conversation, inherit it in a fork, drop it at compaction and clear (TUI) and fire SessionStart compact/clear again. Codex keeps a repeated resume copy beside the first; Claude 2.1.296 drops an identical copy but keeps a different text. --append-system-prompt and Codex developer_instructions are recorded per conversation, so a conversation started without them never gets them on resume: hook chosen, no argv change. Binding key agent_hint {conversation_id, revision} carried by lifecycle resume; fork inherits from its source binding. Opt-out: HGS_AGENT_HINT=0, HGS_AGENT_HINT_OFF account IDs. tests/test_agent_hint_native.py: one hint per request across start, compact, clear, two resumes, rename, fork and a pre-hint conversation; red on main dfe25722 ([0] != [1]) and on an always-emit mutant for Codex ([2] != [1]). title: Add hgs guide and hgs self for agent coordination
description: Progressive-disclosure tier of the parent epic: an on-demand compact guide compiled into hgs and a verified self-identity command that the static hint and the sender envelope rely on.
design:
`hgs [@host] guide [topic]`: static text compiled into the binary. The base page (<= ~600 tokens, enforced by a byte-size test) covers identity (hgs self), ls/inspect, guarded send JSON shape and the never-resend-uncertain rule, how to reply, the wait protocol pointer, detached launch with --launch-id and ended_launches, and pause vs kill vs archive. Destructive operations (kill, stopping another owner's session) require explicit owner authorization; prefer pause. It also covers @host routing and the `hgs @host -h` capability probe. Topics: send, wait, launch, stop, remote. It routes over SSH like other read-only commands.

`hgs self --json`: resolve the caller through native process ancestry (session_graph::sends::send_origin), returning current name, machine UUID and route name, run_id, conversation_id and the same zerus:// reference `hgs reference` produces. After a rename it must find the binding by run identity instead of the stale HGS_SESSION. Unattributed callers (GUI/connector subprocesses, plain shells) get a clear nonzero error.
acceptance_criteria:
- guide base page and each topic stay under their byte budgets (tests); text is English and contains no paths or identifiers.
- `hgs @peer guide` returns the peer's guide; an older peer yields the normal unknown-command error.
- self returns the post-rename name, matches `hgs reference` output, and rejects callers without verified ancestry.
- docs/reference.md documents both commands.
notes: Implemented on branch feat/agent-guide-self, PR #212 (commit ca17b8b7). hgs guide index is 1415 bytes (~350 tokens); topics send/wait/launch/stop. Remote guide uses the same help probe as wait. hgs self reuses the send_origin ancestry proof (owned_record) and follows rename shadows. Local: check-source, clippy 1.99.1 and full scripts/ci/cli.sh passed. Finding for zerus-igb7.2/.3: hgs inspect prints ~146 KB JSON for a busy Claude session, so the guide tells agents to select fields with jq; a compact inspect mode could save more context later.
close_reason: Merged in PR #212 (merge 7776121a): hgs guide [send|wait|launch|stop] and hgs self [--json]; CI gate passed after rerunning the known Windows Qt flake zerus-ssoi.

title: Teach every Zerus-launched agent hgs coordination with minimal context
description: Owner request 2026-10-17: agents in any project, not only the zerus repository through its CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, must know that hgs lets them read, message, launch and stop other Zerus sessions on this and other computers. New sessions should pay the minimum context, and the knowledge must stay correct across resume, unpause, reboot restore, recovery, clear, compaction, fork and rename. Today Zerus injects nothing: agents get only HGS_* environment variables, and hgs send delivers bare text, so a recipient cannot tell another agent wrote it or how to reply.
design:
Progressive disclosure in three tiers, so a new session pays about 40 tokens once and the rest only when an agent actually coordinates.

1. Static hint, delivered to every agent hgs starts. One English sentence, at most ~50 tokens, byte-identical for every session and hgs version: no session name, ID, machine, version or path. Byte stability keeps prompt caches warm across resumes and upgrades and makes the hint rename-safe. Draft: "You are running in a Zerus session: the `hgs` CLI reads, messages, launches and stops other agent sessions on this and other computers; run `hgs guide` before using it."
2. `hgs [@host] guide [topic]`: a compact cheat sheet compiled into the binary (base page <= ~600 tokens; topics send, wait, launch, stop, remote for depth). It is version-matched by construction; `@host` returns that peer's own guide, and the guide tells agents to probe `hgs @host -h` before using commands an older peer may lack. docs/ remains the specification; the guide links to it rather than restating it.
3. `hgs self --json`: the caller's current session name, machine, run and conversation and its copyable zerus:// reference, proven through native process ancestry (reuse session_graph::sends::send_origin). HGS_SESSION is fixed at launch, so this command must resolve the current name after a rename.

Hint delivery chooses, per provider, a native channel that never replaces user instructions and never accumulates in history:
- hgs-owned engines (official DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode native API): add the hint to the instructions hgs already builds.
- Claude Code, Codex, Kimi: preferred channel is the SessionStart hook hgs already installs, returning additional context only for a verified tracked run (works for project launchers too). Emit on startup, clear and compact. On resume, emit only when the binding has no delivery mark for that exact conversation, so pre-feature conversations learn on their next resume and repeated resumes add nothing. Fallback where a hook cannot add context: a launch-time instruction flag merged with any user-supplied value (Claude --append-system-prompt, Codex developer instructions), added on every launch and resume but never saved in the run's base argv. This is the existing statusline pattern in src/state/lifecycle.rs ("The saved base stays as launched; resume adds the settings again").
- Verify each mechanism against the pinned native versions before adoption; when none is verified, skip with a diagnostic instead of guessing.
- Never teach a live agent by sending it a message, never edit user-owned CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and do not target arbitrary commands (hgs sh) or native subagents.

Receiving side: an agent-originated hgs send (attribution already proven by send_origin) wraps its text in one compact envelope carrying the sender's name, machine and zerus:// reference, which is enough for `hgs inspect` and a reply. Owner, desktop and phone sends stay bare. Activity renders the envelope as a peer message (journal::system_prompt already classifies Claude's own cross-session envelopes as peer_message).

Controls: on by default; opt-out in hgs configuration globally and per account. `hgs guide` and `hgs self` always work.

Docs: new reference.md section and agent-coordination.md update; afterwards trim the repository CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md guidance that the hint and guide make redundant (mirror both files).
acceptance_criteria:
- A new agent of every supported provider learns about hgs coordination at a fixed cost of <= ~50 tokens, with no repository instructions.
- Lifecycle matrix verified, each with exactly one hint in effective context: new launch (CLI, desktop, Android, iOS, detached --launch-id), resume/unpause, resume --all after reboot, automatic recovery, archive restore, resume --fresh and live Clear session, native and hgs compaction, fork, rename (hint unchanged, hgs self returns the new name), hgs upgrade between launch and resume, remote launch through a peer.
- Older peers inject nothing and fail no launch; mixed-version guidance is in the guide.
- User instruction flags, project launchers and saved base argv are preserved; opt-out works.
- Recipients of agent-originated sends can identify the sender and reply without other context.

title: Review the GUI's PTY and swarm-worker jobs, which forbid breakaway
description: tray/src/PtyProcess_win.cpp and tray/src/SwarmWorkerSupervisor.cpp put their child in a KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job without BREAKAWAY_OK. A launch, resume or fork that runs from such a child would start a session host that stops in that job and is refused (D4), since the job holds no desktop shell. Check whether any path creates sessions from these children (Open terminal window, resume in a terminal) and, if one does, let that job allow breakaway or start the create outside it. Split from zerus-rwuf.
close_reason: Reviewed; merged in PR #215 (a979316a). The embedded terminal job runs only hgs a --existing, which attaches to a live session through its host, and the swarm worker job never creates sessions, so neither job's forbidden breakaway can place a session host. Comments in PtyProcess_win.cpp and SwarmWorkerSupervisor.cpp keep that rule.

description: 2026-10-17 main CI: run 857 (d039efb9) failed only services/mobile/relay tests/contracts.rs:2765 — the stalled over-limit stream got 429 instead of 413 (timing of the large-payload lane). comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
Root causes and fixes (2026-10-17, Mac worktree, isolated PostgreSQL 17.11 container and offscreen Qt 6.11.2).

Relay: main CI run 39047508658 (#857, d039efb9) attempt 1, job 117439462150, tests/contracts.rs:2765: the stalled over-limit stream got 429 "relay capacity is busy". The test never proved that the stalled request held the single large payload lane before probing. Linux loopback buffers about 2.6 MiB without any server read (measured in a Linux container), more than the 1088 KiB stalled upload, so the writes finish before the relay admits that request and the first probe races its PostgreSQL authentication and rate queries to the lane. A probe holding the lane refuses the stalled stream as busy. macOS buffers about 727 KiB, so its writes wait for relay reads, which is why local runs pass. Deterministic reproduction (scratch, not committed): a probe that holds the lane, confirmed by 100 Continue, followed by the unchanged stalled phase returns exactly the CI 429. Fix (test only): the stalled upload sends Expect: 100-continue and the test probes only after 100 Continue, which hyper 1.12 sends only when App::body first reads the body after taking the lane. Passing: 50/50 runs of the test and 5/5 full contracts runs (8 threads) on PostgreSQL; fmt and clippy clean.

Windows Qt: main runs 39043833088 (#853, 6b69915c) job 117431764887 and 39045559571 (#855, 48f1bcdf) job 117435649155, newMachineDraftCancelAndDiscard(discard): selectedItems().first() != currentItem(). Not event-loop slowness. The phone panel from PR #192 replaces "Checking phones..." with a longer status when its CLI requests finish, shrinking the Machines list (offscreen macOS: 369 to 219 px, 64 px rows). When three rows no longer fit, the draft scrolls the list; Discard rebuilds the rows and the list scrolls back while the click that asked is still pressed, so QAbstractItemView applies the press selection to the row now under its old position (@local) while current is mac. Only Cancel restored the highlight. Product fix in MachinesPage: restore the current row highlight after every row change handled during a press. Test: pin the list to two rows (asserting the scrolled precondition) and wait for the highlight with QTRY instead of qWait(30). Without the fix 3/3 runs fail with "@local" vs "mac"; with it 30/30 focused and 10/10 whole test_machinespage runs pass.

Side note: on this Mac the relay contracts' SQLite fallback fails for every test (Error 503 in the fixture store()), with or without this change; CI runs these contracts only on PostgreSQL.

title: Make CLI lifecycle and transcript polling tests reliable under CI load
description: Release candidate 38908051629 at exact main 48dff262 exposed two intermittent test failures: macOS test_account_lifecycle.test_claude_profile_also_isolates_global_anthropic_config timed out waiting 10 seconds for its fake forked Claude process to exit after SIGTERM; all five executable account lifecycle tests passed locally and the parallel main CI integration step passed. Linux native Claude 2.1.296 test_claude_input_native.test_multiline_message_ending_in_backslashes_is_preserved raised JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string while accepted() read the concurrently written transcript. Investigate the fake-process stop timeout with retained diagnostics and make transcript polling wait for complete appended JSONL records without hiding malformed complete records. Do not change live native agents or reduce compatibility coverage. Stable task zerus-6a2u.19 retains the exact candidate and requires successful rerun gates before publication.
notes:
Exact candidate attempt 2 macOS completed scripts/ci/cli.sh successfully and advanced to the native-agent matrix. The pause/fork timeout did not reproduce; no lifecycle or test source was modified. The separate attempt-2 Linux failure occurred before tests during a concurrent npm upstream publication, not in transcript polling.
Candidate attempt 3 Linux CLI and full native-agent matrix succeeded at unchanged 48dff262. The partial-transcript read error did not recur. Both observed test instabilities remain recorded for dedicated hardening; the release required complete successful gates, without skips or source changes.
2026-10-20 source reconciliation: the partial-JSONL read hardening is already on current main in44bf3d6f (tests/test_claude_questions_native.py records: decode only newline-terminated records, retain malformed-complete-record refusal and U+2028/NEL semantics); tests/test_native_records.py covers it. Transcript polling (2026-10-17): release candidate run 38908051629 attempt 1, Linux job 116996692845, test_claude_input_native.test_multiline_message_ending_in_backslashes_is_preserved raised JSONDecodeError (Unterminated string, column 307) in accepted(): it parsed every line of a transcript that Claude Code was still appending. title: Settings send tests read the fixture input before its Enter arrives
description: tests/test_settings.py test_new_conversation_discards_old_pending_intent and test_pending_settings_apply_before_ready_message compare the fixture agent's received bytes right after hgs send returns. The fixture records the final carriage return after hgs returns, so CI can read the paste without it (PR #157 run 38821503313, CLI ubuntu-24.04: got the paste without the trailing CR). Same race as zerus-kpl4; wait for the CR first.
close_reason: Landed on main in the combined push fab5baad (commit 537f21ad, PR #158 closed as merged).

comments.author: ufna
comments.text:
Timing diagnosis for the #157 failure (run 38821503313, CLI ubuntu-24.04, `test_new_conversation_discards_old_pending_intent` at line 245):

- **Sender:** `hgs send` (`src/state/input.rs` `submit`) pastes the text, sleeps 180 ms, sends Enter as a separate `terminal.send(pane, Enter)` (tmux send-keys writes `\r` into the pane's pty), marks the receipt `submitted` and returns. It never waits for the agent to read that `\r`, and by design it never retries Enter.
- **Enter was sent:** a failed Enter returns `delivery uncertain` with a non-zero exit. The test's `returncode == 0` assertion on line 244 passed, so tmux accepted the Enter.
- **Recorder:** the fixture agent (`tests/test_input.py` `FAKE_AGENT`) is a separate process that `select`s on the pty and appends each `read()` chunk to `received`. Because of the 180 ms gap, the paste and the `\r` arrive as separate reads. The `\r` reaches the file only after the fixture process is scheduled again, which can be after `hgs send` has exited.
- **Observed:** `received` held the full bracketed paste (written 180 ms or more before Enter) and lacked only the trailing `\r`. That matches this window exactly. A transport fault would show a missing or partial paste, or a non-zero exit.
- **#157's source:** its only `input.rs` change is a synchronous `claude_usage_limit::current` guard in `checked_input`, before the paste. It does not touch the paste→Enter path or anything after it.
- **Precedent:** the same race was fixed for the busy send test in #143 (zerus-kpl4). This PR applies the same wait to the remaining two tests that compare `received` right after `hgs send`.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
2026-10-18 read-only Mac App Store feasibility under zerus-pvfa. The owner deferral ("Пока только Homebrew, App Store отложить") stands. No Apple account, legal, App ID, profile or App Store Connect writes were made, and no signing, ID or bundle change. Facts come from current main dfe25722 and the notarized CI bundle 6da797db.

Verified current state:
- hgs-tray (com.hgdev.hgs-tray) is signed with hardened-runtime entitlements only: automation.apple-events, device.camera, device.audio-input. The helpers hgs and zerus-mobile-connector carry no entitlements. There is no com.apple.security.app-sandbox anywhere.
- The bundle ships zerus-setup (a /usr/bin/env python3 script) and Resources/setup/*.py, which write ~/Library/LaunchAgents and link ~/.local/bin/hgs. It also ships Qt and FFmpeg dylibs and plugins, and an in-app updater for Homebrew, DMG and portable installs.
- The iOS client app.zerus.mobile is iPhone-only (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 1), with SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST=NO and SUPPORTS_MAC_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD=NO. ZerusKit's Package.swift already declares .macOS(.v15).

What App Sandbox would break in the current local product:
1. Local agents. hgs runs user-installed provider CLIs and Homebrew tmux. Under the sandbox every child inherits it (embedded helpers need com.apple.security.inherit), so the CLIs cannot read their own home-directory state, repositories outside user-selected folders, or ~/.ssh. Only temporary-exception file entitlements would allow that, and App Review may reject them.
2. Per-user services and shared state. LaunchAgents (autostart, session bridge, recovery, swarm, voice, connector) would have to become bundled SMAppService helpers. ~/.local/bin/hgs for SSH callers, and the shared ~/.config/hgs and ~/.local/state/hgs, would move into the container, where non-sandboxed SSH sessions cannot see them.
3. Open in Terminal (osascript, then Terminal Apple Events) would need com.apple.security.temporary-exception.apple-events for com.apple.Terminal.
4. A sandboxed system ssh cannot read ~/.ssh keys or known_hosts.
5. The in-app, Homebrew and DMG update flows must be absent from a store build; the store manages updates.
6. Its Python setup tools depend on Command Line Tools.

Entitlements a sandboxed store build would declare, by scope:
- Required: com.apple.security.app-sandbox.
- network.client (relay over HTTPS).
- device.audio-input (voice messages), and device.camera if video is kept.
- files.user-selected.read-write plus files.bookmarks.app-scope, only if local folder features are kept.
- inherit on every embedded helper.
- automation.apple-events plus temporary-exception.apple-events, only if Terminal integration is kept (risky).
- The profile-provided application-identifier and team-identifier.

Distribution choices for the owner (decisions; nothing is guessed or created):
A. A remote-client Mac edition: a sandboxed relay client like the iOS app, with no local agents. Needs network.client and audio-input.
   - A1: enable Designed for iPhone/iPad on Mac for app.zerus.mobile (smallest change; an availability setting on the existing record).
   - A2: a native macOS SwiftUI target built on ZerusKit. This needs a bundle ID decision: reuse app.zerus.mobile for universal purchase, or a new ID. Never com.hgdev.hgs-tray, which keeps the notarized Developer ID and TCC identity of the Homebrew/DMG app.
B. A full local-agent edition inside the sandbox: not feasible without redesigning agent execution, tmux, SSH and the services. Not recommended.
C. Keep Homebrew plus the DMG (Developer ID) as the only local-agent distribution, with the store used only for A.

Open owner/legal items, untouched:
- Qt and FFmpeg licensing under App Store terms (only relevant to a Qt-based store build, not A).
- App Store Connect agreements, privacy labels and export compliance.
- Whether to resume zerus-8reb at all.

title: Investigate Android Markdown cache entry-budget CI race
description: Main CI38723363544 at8b55892 failed MarkdownDocumentCacheTest.entryBudgetEvictsTheLeastRecentlyUsedExactDocument at line110 (entry count assertion);702 JVM tests,one failure. Desktop Qt gates passed. No Android source in that Worktrees layout commit or the current desktop-only cache feature. Reproduce exact cache completion/retention ordering under concurrency before changing production semantics or fixture assertions; retain LRU/byte/admission tests. This is a separate automatic Dev publication gate finding, not evidence against desktop cache qualification.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #220 (merge e486d9fa): a finished Markdown flight now leaves the flight table under the cache lock before its job completes, so await() returning before the completion handler can no longer let a later request join it. CI gate green on head 94bc7338, including the Android unit tests.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
Root cause and fix (2026-10-17).

Hosted failures: main run 38723363544 (#517, 8b55892c) job 116383203672 entryBudgetEvictsTheLeastRecentlyUsedExactDocument; main run 38614726583 (#451, 6ed81bcb) job 116030186398 and PR run 38533973327 (#402, 5c151c1f) job 115752313594 byteBudgetCountsModelWeightAndDoesNotRetainOversizedDocuments. Gradle reports each test's runBlocking line (110, 123), not the failing assertion.

Cause (production race, not the fixture): MarkdownDocumentCache removed a finished flight from `flights` only in the deferred's invokeOnCompletion handler. kotlinx.coroutines 1.10.2 publishes the completed state (tryFinalizeSimpleState) before completeStateFinalization runs the handlers, so await() on another thread can return in between. A sequential next request for a source that was not retained (oversized "large") or was evicted ("b") then found the stale completed flight and returned it without parsing, so calls was 3 instead of 4.

Fix: the flight leaves `flights` inside its own body, under the same lock as the cache insert or drop, before the deferred completes. The completion handler still releases the permit and covers cancellation. LRU, byte and admission semantics and tests are unchanged; the budget tests also assert that a finished request leaves no flight.

Evidence (this Mac lacks JDK 17/21 and SDK 36, so the real production file and test class were compiled with kotlinc 2.1.20, kotlinx-coroutines 1.10.2, commonmark 0.30.0 and JUnit 4.13.2 on the JVM, under CPU contention): the CI scenarios on the original code failed 3/20000 and 2/100000 runs with calls=3 (0/300000 in a quieter run); the real MarkdownDocumentCacheTest on the original code failed 1/40000 runs (the new inFlightCount check), and 0/40000 with the fix; fixed scenarios 0/300000. The interleaving lives inside kotlinx completion, so no unit test can force it without a production hook; the fix removes the dependence by construction.

title: Desktop: a peer whose HGS_SELF differs from its machine alias never connects and keeps a stale error
description: Interactive check 2026-10-14, reproducible on any platform. Machine alias winpeer, peer HGS_SELF=zpeer. HgsClient::requestPeer runs 'hgs @winpeer ls --json', parses host=zpeer, and TrayAgent::onPeerReady removes m_pollingHosts[zpeer] (not winpeer) and then drops the reply because peers does not contain zpeer. Result: the banner keeps 'winpeer: Host key verification failed. (retrying…)' or 'connecting…' forever, the machine stays Not connected and its sessions never appear, while Test connection reports Connected. Setting HGS_SELF=winpeer on the peer fixes it. Expected: key the polled box by the alias the GUI asked for (or report the mismatch).
notes: 2026-10-14, PR #62 zip on Windows: alias winpeer, peer HGS_SELF=zpeer; the peer connects at once and its session is listed under winpeer with no error banner.
close_reason: Fixed in #62 (2f04f03): peer answers are keyed by the polled alias (reported name kept in BoxState::reportedHost); polling state comes from HgsClient. Verified on Windows with alias winpeer and HGS_SELF=zpeer.

title: Windows: Ctrl+C and other control keys do not reach Codex 0.162 through the session host
description: Found by the real-agent Windows suite (tests/test_windows_native_agents.py, NativeWindowsCodex.test_input_keys_reach_codex_through_the_host; the spike S2 checks folded in from zerus-ziq3.7.13) on the Windows test PC, Codex 0.162.0 win32, bundled ConPTY, twice. Sent through hgs __host backend op send: a lone Esc then literal text arrives whole ('esc probe' shows in the composer), but a single Ctrl+C (C-c, 0x03) leaves the draft in place for 120 s, and C-e C-u do not clear it either. The record stays activity unknown with no error. The same keys work for Claude Code 2.1.296 through the same host path: Ctrl+C clears its draft, C-e C-u clear it, and text typed after Ctrl+S shows. Spike S2 saw Codex not clear on raw ConPTY too. S2 measured Codex's console input mode as 0x0098 (no ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, no ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT), so crossterm reads INPUT_RECORDs, and how ConPTY turns C0 bytes into key events (virtual key and LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED) decides whether Codex sees Ctrl+letter. Determine what Codex receives and fix the host's key encoding for agents without VT input (for example, write KEY_EVENTs with the control state for named C-x keys) so that Ctrl+C clears or interrupts Codex as in a real console. Blocks closing zerus-ziq3.7.13 and gating windows-host.
notes:
Hypothesis (2026-10-14, host side): Codex's console input mode 0x0098 (S2) has neither ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT nor ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, so it reads INPUT_RECORDs and ConPTY turns a raw C0 byte (0x03, 0x15) written by the host into a key event without LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED, which crossterm does not read as Ctrl+letter. Both ConPTY builds ask the terminal for win32-input-mode (DECSET 9001, S1); the host strips it (src/host/sequences.rs) and writes plain VT input. Candidate fix: encode Ctrl+letter (from named keys and from attach clients' C0 bytes) as win32-input-mode sequences CSI Vk;Sc;Uc;Kd;Cs;Rc _ with the Ctrl state, as Windows Terminal does once 9001 is requested; ConPTY turns them back into VT for apps that read VT input (Claude, Kimi). Probe with real Codex and Claude (raw vs win32 C-c and C-u) prepared for the Windows PC.
Root cause confirmed 2026-10-14 by probe on the Windows PC (real Codex 0.162.0 and Claude Code 2.1.296 through the host, bundled ConPTY): crossterm on Windows (src/event/sys/windows/parse.rs) resolves a key event whose u_char is a control character (< 0x20) with ToUnicodeEx in the keyboard layout of the foreground window; the PC's active layout is Russian, so Ctrl+C reaches Codex as Ctrl+'с' (Cyrillic) and Codex ignores it. Raw 0x03 and win32-input-mode with Uc=3 both fail; win32-input-mode with no Ctrl typed 'с'. A win32-input-mode key with the Latin letter as Uc (CSI 67;46;99;1;8;1_ then ...;0;8;1_) clears Codex's composer for Ctrl+C and Ctrl+U, and Claude (VT input) still clears with every form. Hosted CI runners with a US layout may not show the bug. Fix: the host encodes Ctrl+letter (named keys and attach clients' C0 bytes, outside escape sequences and bracketed paste) as win32-input-mode keys with the Latin letter and LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED while the console has requested DECSET 9001.
Fix up as PR #54 (2026-10-14, branch p2/win32-ctrl-keys): while the console has requested DECSET 9001, the host sends a lone Ctrl+letter (0x01-0x1A except BS/TAB/LF/CR), from backend key sends and from attach clients' typed input, as win32-input-mode key-down/up records with the Latin letter and LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED; pastes, escape sequences and query replies stay raw. Verified on the Windows PC: named C-c and C-u clear the draft in real Codex 0.162.0 and Claude 2.1.296.
PR #54 first version regressed VT-input consoles in hosted CI (fake agent got 'c' for C-c; ConPTY turns a win32 key record into its Uc for a console with ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT; real Claude passed only because libuv reads key records). Rework: convert hgs's own key sends only when the supervisor reports the agent's console input mode without VT input (Codex 0x0098); attach typing stays raw, as any native terminal sends it (Codex under a non-Latin layout then behaves as in Windows Terminal, an upstream crossterm limitation). Product path: input_queue.rs sends C-s for 'ctrl-s to steer immediately'.
close_reason: Merged in PR #54: Ctrl+letter key sends reach a key-record console (Codex) as win32-input-mode records with the Latin letter; verified on the Windows PC with real Codex and Claude and the real-agent suite (6/6 each)

title: Windows: hgs answer leaves a Codex async question reply unsubmitted in the composer
description: Found by the real-agent Windows suite (tests/test_windows_native_agents.py, NativeWindowsCodex.test_hgs_answers_request_user_input_async; zerus-ziq3.7.12) on the Windows test PC, twice, with Codex 0.162.0 win32 through the session host (bundled ConPTY). Codex calls request_user_input_async from the fake API and its turn ends, so the panel is gone and codex_questions::answer takes the input::submit path with the <send_user_message_question_reply> envelope (multi-line JSON). hgs answer returns status 'submitted' (the 6 s confirmation wait expires). The captured screen 120 s later still shows the whole envelope in Codex's composer, the fake API never receives a fourth request, and the record keeps input_pending_at. So the paste arrived but its Enter did not submit. On Linux the same case passes. Plain hgs send messages, including a short multiline one, submit fine through the host, so suspect the longer multi-line paste: Enter 180 ms after it (spike S2 criterion d) may still fall inside Codex's Windows paste-burst handling, or ConPTY may deliver the paste in pieces. Reproduce with the suite on Windows; check what Codex receives (bracketed paste vs key events) and whether hgs should wait for a settled composer before Enter or resend Enter after verifying the draft.
notes: Root cause (2026-10-14, from Codex tui/src/bottom_pane/paste_burst.rs): chars <=8 ms apart form a paste burst (60 ms idle timeout on Windows) and an Enter within PASTE_ENTER_SUPPRESS_WINDOW = 120 ms of the last burst char inserts a newline. Codex on Windows reads console key events (no VT input, mode 0x0098 in S2), so ConPTY delivers hgs's bracketed paste as typed keys; the 210-byte reply is still being processed when hgs's Enter arrives at its fixed 180 ms. Candidate fix on branch p2/codex-paste-enter (4a8da2d): for Codex on Windows, poll the plain capture until the composer shows the whole paste (or Codex's [Pasted Content placeholder), within 2 s + 4 ms/byte, then 200 ms, then the single Enter; Unix keeps 180 ms. Verification requested from the native-suite session on the Windows PC.
close_reason: Merged in PR #48 (verified with the real-agent Windows suite)

title: durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive(send-expiry) hung a Windows sessionswindow shard
description: Trusted main run 38523322814 at be17b70 (Windows client, desktop and portable zip, job 115719062635): CTest killed sessionswindow-0 after 240 s. The shard's output ends at QWARN for TestSessionsWindow::durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive(send-expiry) with no PASS/FAIL, so the process hung without a QTRY timeout firing, which suggests the GUI thread was blocked. The test holds the draft store's first write on a semaphore (ComposerDraftStore::setWriteObserver: entered.release(); release.acquire()) and only releases it after the warm-cache expiry deadline passes (QTRY_VERIFY on currentSecsSinceEpoch() >= expires_at). Hypothesis to check first: some path the GUI thread takes while the write is held (expiry handling, a re-render or draft save) waits synchronously for the writer (flushWrites or similar), so the test's own block deadlocks the GUI. If so, determine whether a real slow disk could do the same to the product (GUI blocked until a write completes) or whether only the test's indefinite block can. The rows did not change in PR #44; the failed jobs were re-run to see whether it repeats.
notes: Cause confirmed: the expiry rows set a warm cache until now + 2 whole seconds; if the cache expired before the click (slow details.json replacement on Windows), admission opened the modal coldCacheConfirm / questionColdCacheConfirm and nothing answered it. A 2.1 s QTest::qSleep before the click hangs the unpatched row deterministically on Linux (rc 124, no output, like CI). Not a product deadlock: the draft store's observer runs outside its mutex and no GUI path calls the blocking store helpers. Fix in PR #47: now + 4, a 10 s expiry wait, and a zero-timer guard that rejects either confirmation and fails the row with a message.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #47 (e241318), test only. The expiry rows gave the warm cache as little as 1 s before the click; an expired cache at admission opened the modal cold-cache confirmation that nothing answered, hanging the shard. Now now + 4 (at least 3 s), a 10 s expiry wait, and a zero-timer guard that rejects either confirmation and fails with a message. Injected 2.1 s delay: unpatched hangs (rc 124, as on CI), patched passes; 4.1 s: patched fails fast. Windows test PC: patched 96/96 send-expiry, 48/48 question-expiry, 16/16 all rows, no hangs; PR CI run 38526727144 green.

title: hgs terminate on Windows refuses while the host still lists the ended session
description: Found by the terminal backend contract against the session host (PR #41, hosted Windows CI run 38511780818, job 115681739103): test_terminate_waits_for_the_agent_then_archives_the_session got 'hgs: session is still running; its saved binding was kept'. Not reproduced in 4 runs on the Windows test PC, so it is timing dependent. Path (src/state/terminate.rs): after kill_session, terminate waits only for the agent process to exit, then takes the state lock and checks live(). On the host the session stays listed until its --run supervisor has run supervisor::finish (which needs that same state lock), exited and been drained by the host (registry::ended), so live() can still contain the name. On tmux kill-session removes it at once. Expected (contract): 'hgs: terminated and archived NAME (...)', the agent ended by the close signals, the session archived. Candidate fix: on the host, wait (bounded by the existing deadline) until the backend no longer lists the session before taking the lock and checking live(), so the supervisor can finish; keep the safety checks and the 'archived' path if the supervisor archived first. The same window may affect kill and pause listing (contract review).
notes: Fix up as PR #43 (2026-10-14): on Windows terminate waits, without the state lock and within its 20 s deadline, until the host no longer lists the terminated run, so the supervisor can record the exit and end; Unix makes no extra tmux call. Pause already waits unlocked; kill does not check the listing afterwards.
close_reason: Fixed by the Phase 2 owner session in PR #43 (043a3b4): Windows terminate waits for the listing without holding the lock. Verified by the host backend contract suite (PR #41, merged 88cdd3f): test_terminate_waits_for_the_agent_then_archives_the_session and the other 11 cases passed 4/4 rounds on the Windows test PC and in hosted Windows CI run 38514919925.

title: Qualify coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation on Windows
description: PR #40 Windows CI run 38506309544 (job 115664554827), a packaging change that does not touch the desktop, failed TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation: 'shown' returned FALSE at tray/tests/test_sessionswindow.cpp(1774). The macOS crash of the same test (zerus-c9p) was fixed and closed; this is the Windows form. Reproduce with loaded parallel runs on the Windows PC (as for zerus-0jix/a0ak, 48 parallel processes) and fix with an exact barrier without weakening the draft and conversation-pin assertions.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #44 (be17b70), test only. Cause: on Windows, Qt 6.10 runs a coarse timer of 20 ms or less as a multimedia timer that posts its QTimerEvent (qeventdispatcher_win.cpp), so the test's 5 ms confirmation timer shared a sendPostedEvents() batch with queued ProcessRunner replies. The reply of the window's show-time inspection, which had read the old conversation, could be delivered after the accept and before exec() returned. It restored conversation-cache, the second confirmation started a send, and the third click found a disabled button ('shown' FALSE at 1774). The product stays safe: the payload pins expected_conversation_id. Fix: setDetailsPollForTests(500, 24 h); wait (15 s) for the reply to the test's own inspection, and for the reply to the inspection started by the conversation change; assert !isSending after each refused confirmation. Reproduced on Linux with timing injection (original 16/16 fail, fixed 24/24 + 120/120 under load). Windows test PC: unpatched 96/96 (not reproduced there), fixed 96/96 including a round on a freshly built binary; hosted CI run 38521674575 green.

title: test_account_mcp temp directory still written at teardown on macOS
description: PR #32 macOS CLI job 115573880968: test_account_mcp.ManagedProfileMcp.test_claude_and_kimi_profiles_receive_native_servers errored in TemporaryDirectory cleanup with OSError [Errno 66] Directory not empty: .../zerus-mcp-*. Something (a background process or a late write by hgs or a fixture) still writes into the temporary directory after the test body. Find the writer and make the test wait for it or stop it before cleanup, without hiding a product process that outlives its command.
notes: 2026-10-14 second symptom (PR #33 Ubuntu CLI, parser-only change): test_claude_and_kimi_profiles_receive_native_servers (agent='kimi') got empty output from self.launch(agent): json.loads raised JSONDecodeError at char 0 (tests/test_account_mcp.py:79). close_reason: Merged in PR #36 (533485f): test_account_mcp stops its private tmux server and waits for the pane processes (hgs --run supervisors, matched by start time, ps with separate -o options that read the same under POSIX and procps) before removing its directory, and the fakes publish their observation file by rename. Covers both hosted symptoms (macOS Directory not empty at cleanup, Ubuntu empty launch output).

title: subagent descriptor is corrupt while polling DeepSeek child events
description: PR #32 Ubuntu CLI job 115573881072: test_dsh_native.NativeHarness.test_child_activity_requires_exact_parent_and_keeps_public_history failed at tests/test_dsh_native.py:360 because an hgs call polling child events returned 'hgs: subagent descriptor is corrupt'. Likely a reader seeing a descriptor while it is written (non-atomic write or a read of a partially replaced file). Find the writer and reader, decide whether the product must write atomically or the reader must treat an incomplete descriptor as not yet available, and fix the root cause.
close_reason: Merged in PR #35 (6739669): a starting one-shot DeepSeek child (cataloged by its parent before its first step records subagent/descriptor) now shows an empty, unsendable page instead of the native 'subagent descriptor is corrupt'; a descriptor recorded meanwhile gets one native retry, and wrong parents or stored children without a descriptor keep the native error. title: Decide how the desktop opens executable attachments
description: Attachment chips and Activity attachments open cached copies with QDesktopServices::openUrl, i.e. the platform default handler. Files written by Zerus carry no download origin marker, so an attachment received from a remote conversation with an executable or shell-handled type (for example .exe, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .url, .scf on Windows; .command or .app bundles on macOS; .desktop on Linux) is handed to the system with no additional prompt. zerus-fn6d removed only the .lnk case, because Qt also mis-validated it. Decide the product behaviour, for example: reveal in the file manager instead of opening, require a confirmation that names the type, or mark the cached copy with the platform's downloaded-file origin. Then apply it to AttachmentLoader::open and MessageComposer::openAttachment consistently, with tests per platform.
close_reason: Owner chose browser-like opening. Files from other machines carry the platform downloaded-file marker (Windows Mark of the Web, macOS quarantine); anything that would run a program is selected in the file manager instead of opened, on every platform (tray/src/ExternalFile). title: Expose definitive voice rejection and safe resubmission states
description: Distinguish a verified pre-acceptance rejection from transport uncertainty using structured request/run/conversation-bound JSON responses. design: Plan: durable pre-acceptance refusal barrier in the voice store, keyed by original native message UUID and normalized immutable request digest. Resubmission uses a fresh transport operation UUID plus the original native message UUID and one scoped refusal generation/token, so old envelopes remain blocked and existing native message/receipt IDs stay unchanged. description: Review zerus-pta0: SessionList.cpp:29-40 invalidates each full visible working row every 80 ms, although workingPulse changes only the status indicator/counter. An isolated eight-row fixture at 2x scale produces 25 paints and 6.78 million logical dirty pixels in two seconds, costing 32 ms thread CPU; disabling activity animation produces zero paints in the same static fixture. Optimize indicator/counter repaint bounds or cache static row content, and qualify input/paint latency with many active rows under load. This is avoidable steady work, not independently proven to cause the reported full freeze.

Invalidate only changing regions and skip static delegate drawing where clipped indicator-only painting reproduces the full frame. Preserve existing transition composition, themes, DPR, compact rows and elapsed-width changes. Avoid new bitmap caches when exact clipped painting suffices.
notes: Implemented shared pulse/counter/elapsed geometry and narrow dirty regions with clipped delegate painting. Pixel parity covers themes, compact rows, children, elapsed-width boundaries and DPR 1/1.25/1.5/2. Eight-row 2x fixture reduced dirty bounding area by 96 percent and GUI CPU from 40.2 ms to 10.6 ms. Paintcache and full relevant Qt qualification pass on macOS and Arch. This removes avoidable steady work; the original sustained live freeze was not captured. Qualified source change; installed GUI not updated.

title: Desktop reply banners fire for Kimi scheduled cron ticks and lost focus/idle gating
description: On macOS, each routine reply from a Kimi recurring cron job (CronCreate */15) posts a 'Zerus — New reply' banner. Two causes, verified 2026-10-11: (1) the zerus-vww8 idle gating and zerus-w9sm application-focus suppression were only hot-patched into installed GUI binaries and never committed; installing main 3901833 (0.41.0) on Linux and macOS removed them (installed binaries no longer import QGuiApplication::applicationState). (2) Even with idle gating, a cron-fired Kimi turn ends fully idle (activity/phase idle, no children), so every scheduled tick is a banner-eligible reply. Kimi 2.1.1 sends originKind=cron_job/cron_missed in its TurnStarted hook and journals cron.add/cron.delete in wire.jsonl; hgs drops both. Expected: re-land focus suppression and idle gating; scheduled-tick replies stay unread but do not banner while the scheduled job remains, and the final reply after the job is removed still notifies.
notes:
Follow-up 2026-10-11: owner reported the 21:30 tick still 'notified'. Notification Center showed no Zerus banner after the 21:24 Mac deploy; the remaining signal was the unread mark/badge, which the first fix intentionally kept. Now hgs does not advance reply_id for scheduled ticks while recurring_schedules > 0, and a read reply never moves back behind the read mark during skipping (transition from pre-origin journal rows).
Original implementation (55bc4e4): hgs journals Kimi TurnStarted origin_kind as turn_origin; Kimi sessions report recurring_schedules folded from wire.jsonl cron.add/cron.delete (one-shot excluded; null while unknown); AttentionTracker re-lands zerus-w9sm focus suppression and zerus-vww8 idle gating and consumes scheduled replies silently while recurring jobs remain. Validation: Rust unit tests, scripts/ci/cli.sh (63 modules, 0 failed), all 52 Qt CTest suites, installed on Linux and macOS with native identities and drafts unchanged; 21:30 tick verified reply_scheduled=true without a Notification Center banner.
close_reason: Fixed in 55bc4e4 and d8ceeab; installed on Linux and macOS. Live: the 21:30 tick reported reply_scheduled without a Notification Center banner, and after d8ceeab the 21:45 tick left reply_id on the read reply (no unread mark, badge or banner).

description: test_mobile_worktrees_transport.WorktreeTransport.test_late_dispatch_target_cleans_after_gateway_deadline failed once on CI (ubuntu-24.04) in run 38122605296 (b634f8a, which only changed test timing elsewhere): 'late target Git/native process survived its own mobile budget' at tests/test_mobile_worktrees_transport.py:43 after the 9 s wait; the message does not say whether the post-checkout hook or the late remote native hgs survived. notes: 2026-10-11 root cause: test helper, not the connector. The CI test lasted 35.2 s, so the wait loop ended early when both processes looked dead (zombies, ~t35) and the immediate re-check in assertFalse saw one as alive. Linux briefly reports state X (dead) while a parent reaps a zombie; MobilePeers.running() treated anything but Z as running. Probe on Arch (5000 reaps): Z->X->gone in 479 cases, 477 dead-then-alive flips with the old rule, 0 when X counts as dead. Locally the mobile budget kills the hook and late native hgs at ~t36 against a t39 window (24/24 loaded runs). Fix: treat X like Z in running() and the four other test zombie checks (test_process_control single-shot check, test_input/test_pause/test_mobile_worktrees_native wait loops).
close_reason: Fixed in 5eed3d3: process-state test checks treat X (dead) like Z; CLI (ubuntu-24.04) and CLI (macos-15) passed in run 38124360082, which includes it.

Shared tools such as project memory are therefore missing in every new profile. At each managed launch, merge the native user-level MCP server definitions into the profile (Claude ~/.claude.json mcpServers, Codex config.toml mcp_servers, Kimi mcp.json mcpServers). Use a three-way merge against the last inherited baseline so servers a profile added, changed or removed itself win. Store only digests in the baseline. Provider credentials and hooks stay unshared.

close_reason: Managed Codex, Claude and Kimi launches merge the user's native MCP servers into the profile with a digest-only three-way baseline; profile overrides win and provider sign-in/hooks stay separate. Verified by unit tests, an end-to-end launch test for all three providers that fails without the hook, and the account suites.
