title: Show repository publication status on session cards
description:
## Summary
The owner wants the session card to show whether work has been pushed because local-only work has nearly been lost. Design a compact repository/branch publication indicator beside the existing project/branch line, distinguishing tracked and untracked working changes, commits ahead of the tracked remote, absent upstream and stale or unavailable remote verification. Status belongs to the actual session folder and branch and can be shared by several sessions; do not imply feature ownership or completed remote backup from a stale local ref.

## Acceptance Criteria
A reviewable design shows local changes and unpublished commits separately, with repository identity, remote/upstream and last verification in details. Synced requires adequate current evidence. Non-Git folders, worktrees, detached HEAD, divergent branches and offline machines have explicit states. No automatic commit, push, discard or cleanup. Implement after the product design is agreed.
design: The owner approved the trial on 2026-10-10. Implemented native outline diff, upload, download and cloud check/question icons beside the project/branch line. Distinct counters preserve local file changes and outgoing/incoming commits, with conflict color and exact hover details. Publication verification is read-only and separate from fleet/agent polling; local tracking refs alone never imply a verified remote. Worktrees use their own checkout identity; archives and ordinary non-Git folders have no live publication badge. See docs/reference.md for evidence, refresh, expiration and compatibility behavior.
notes:
Implemented and validated locally without committing or publishing this trial. Rust 1.85: 196 unit tests passed. Ten isolated real-Git publication contracts and 16 existing worktree contracts passed. Qt client/workspace suites passed (74 and 16 cases); integrated session-card checks passed, including shared-folder deduplication, unchanged draft/selection/focus, both themes and 280/360/500 px layouts. Desktop builds and source/privacy checks passed. Native Qt previews are in /tmp/zerus-git-status-preview.
Owner explicitly authorized commit and push on 2026-10-10. Publication is scoped to Git status badges and their read-only backend; other active work is excluded.
Owner-authorized publication completed on 2026-10-10: commit a753770 is pushed to origin/main after rebasing onto concurrent reviewed main updates. The exact integrated revision builds the desktop and passes 198 Rust 1.85 unit tests, 10 isolated Git publication contracts, all 23 worktree contracts, Qt client/workspace suites (74/16 passes including setup and cleanup), and focused integrated window checks (6 passes). Source/privacy gates pass; drafts, selection and editor focus are preserved.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified the owner-approved trial with native icons, independent bounded read-only Git evidence and Qt previews.

title: Separate session-limit recovery with reset-time and interval policies
description:
## Summary
A confirmed Claude session limit with a reset time currently enters the temporary rate-limit retry schedule. Add a distinct session_limit class with a default wait-for-reset policy and an optional per-class delay sequence using existing recovery syntax. Parse native reset evidence with its event time and timezone, preserve manual handling of permanent quota/billing/authentication failures, and expose settings and waiting status.

## Acceptance Criteria
Existing policies migrate without losing schedules. Session-limit recovery defaults to the known reset deadline, supports interval retries, and safely handles missing reset evidence. Tests cover native classification/reset extraction, policy compatibility, cancellation, class switching and settings round trips. Update reference documentation.
notes:
Implemented session_limit recovery policy v3 with default reset mode and optional independent interval schedule (300,0 fallback), native error/reset normalization, legacy episode migration, shared Qt settings and reset status. Verified 195 Rust tests on Rust 1.85, 13 isolated recovery integration tests, focused Qt recovery/settings/quota regressions (9 passes including setup/cleanup), source/privacy checks and dependency notice collection. Qt qualification used a temporary HEAD tray checkout with only this feature overlaid because existing in-progress zerus-6i4u changes have undefined Start fresh methods in the working tree. No commit, deployment or remote sync.
Owner-authorized publication completed on 2026-10-10: commit 2e28c15 is pushed to origin/main. The exact staged source tree builds hgs-tray and passes 193 Rust tests on Rust 1.85, 13 private recovery integration tests and the focused Qt recovery/settings/quota suite (9 passes including setup/cleanup), plus source/privacy checks. The lower Rust count excludes the separate in-progress Start fresh work. Unrelated working changes remain local. Repository publication indicators are tracked separately in zerus-l8v7.
close_reason: Implemented and verified reset/interval session-limit recovery, legacy policy/episode compatibility, native deadline extraction, synchronized settings and UI regressions. Working tree remains uncommitted.

title: Resumed Codex sessions cannot Clear or Pause before their first turn
description: After hgs resume, Codex defers SessionStart until the next user turn, so the binding keeps expected_id. clear_context::available and lifecycle::safe_to_pause both require an empty expected_id, so Clear and Pause stay disabled even when resume_input::ready verifies the owned rollout and an empty composer. Users who resume only to clear must send a message with the full context first. Allowing a verified pending resume to clear or pause needs hook handling for a clear SessionStart while expected_id is set and isolated real-Codex contract coverage. Workaround: resume --fresh from the stopped state (zerus-6i4u).
notes: Fix up as PR #57 (2026-10-14): verified pending Codex resumes may clear and pause before SessionStart; native contracts on Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0.
close_reason: Merged in PR #57 (verified with the pinned real Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0)

title: Research anonymous Android dev distribution and update delivery
description: Compare primary-source options for public APK downloads without tester registration, publishing APIs and in-app update checks. Assess Android installation constraints, signing continuity, current developer verification rollout, and recommend a Zerus dev distribution architecture. Research only; no runtime implementation or deployment.
notes: Research completed 2026-10-09 from primary sources. Recommendation (not yet an implementation decision): public static HTTPS channel manifest plus immutable signed APKs on existing hosting; GitHub prereleases as archive/mirror; optional Obtainium deep link. No user authentication for metadata/downloads, publisher credentials kept private. Native Android PackageInstaller supports conditional self-updates without user action on Android 12+, with install-source approval, current target API and UPDATE_PACKAGES_WITHOUT_USER_ACTION; always handle STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION. GitHub releases/latest excludes prereleases and public REST calls are limited to 60/hour per originating IP; Actions artifacts require sign-in. Obtainium and own F-Droid binary repos offer account-free client-managed updates. Appcircle public testing links support auth=None; its in-app update API is a separate Enterprise App Store feature. Diawi expiration/installation limits suit temporary handoffs. Expo EAS internal URLs permit anonymous access by default. Firebase requires tester Google sign-in; App Center distribution is retired. Current Google FAQ explicitly exempts direct sideloading from the September 2026 initial participating-store rollout; prepare for the announced 2027 expansion. Local source: pilot is nondebuggable but still uses debug signingConfig, no updater/installer permissions implemented. Public APK HEAD was HTTP 200 without credentials. Signing continuity and existing installed data must be preserved before broad distribution. Sources: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageInstaller.SessionParams ; https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/faq ; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases ; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api ; https://wiki.obtainium.imranr.dev/app_tracking/ ; https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Setup_an_F-Droid_App_Repo/ ; https://docs.appcircle.io/testing-distribution/create-or-select-a-distribution-profile ; https://docs.appcircle.io/enterprise-app-store/in-app-updates ; https://www.diawi.com/features-services ; https://docs.expo.dev/build/internal-distribution/ ; https://firebase.google.com/docs/app-distribution/get-set-up-as-a-tester?platform=android ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/appcenter/distribution/uploading . title: Claude task notifications appear as user messages in Activity
description: When a background command finishes, Claude Code starts a new turn whose prompt is a raw <task-notification> XML envelope and fires UserPromptSubmit with it (verified with Claude 2.1.294 against a local fake API; the hook input has no origin field, while the transcript marks promptSource=system, origin.kind=task-notification). HGS journals it as UserPromptSubmit, so Activity renders it as 'You ... Sent' with literal tags, and the session prompt is overwritten. Keep the turn lifecycle, but journal and render it as a system notice with the summary, and do not replace the user's last prompt. Already journaled rows should render correctly too.
notes: Done in working tree: journal::task_notification parses Claude's <task-notification> envelope(s); log_event and journal reads mark such UserPromptSubmit/Queued/TurnStarted rows with origin=task_notification, task_status and the summary as detail (legacy rows too). The turn lifecycle is unchanged, but record.prompt is not overwritten and user_prompt() hides legacy notification prompts from summaries/inspect/search. Search maps notices to role event and skips Claude transcript user turns with origin.kind=task-notification. Activity renders a violet 'Background task' card (dark #c5a8f5/#2a2536, light #6c43b8/#f4f0fb).

title: Claude subagent hand-backs appear as user messages in Activity

(transcript attachment queued_command, origin.kind=peer, handback=true, isMeta=true) and fires UserPromptSubmit with it. HGS journals it as the person's message, so Activity shows 'You ... Sent' with the raw envelope. Extend the task notification handling (zerus-9rz) to agent-message envelopes: keep the turn lifecycle, show a subagent report notice instead of You, render the report as agent Markdown, and keep it out of the session prompt and user-role search.
notes: Done in working tree: journal::system_prompt parses <task-notification> and <agent-message from=...> envelopes (hand-back frame stripped, 2-space report indentation removed). mark_system_prompt sets origin=subagent_report, detail 'Agent "<description>" finished' (description captured at SubagentStart from the single unclaimed active Agent/Task call), report (<=32000 chars) and from_agent. title: Support native DeepSeek context reset when available
description:
## Summary

Clear context is intentionally disabled for DeepSeek because the integrated native SessionController has no supported reset method. Add a capability-gated native reset when the upstream interface supports it. Preserve conversation identity and never truncate provider-owned history or replace a running agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.
close_reason: Not supported by the pinned @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2: no SessionController reset method, no native /clear or /new command, no runtime context-reset event (static API and isolated keyless probe). Clear stays an explicit refusal, pinned by a test in PR #129; revisit when the upstream canary reports a newer dsh.

title: Avoid executing custom launchers during capability detection
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run the custom-launcher cases in tests/test_pause.py.

## Actual Behavior

The Codex capability probe in src/state/lifecycle.rs invokes the configured executable with --help before a supervised run exists. Custom launchers may block, exit, or produce side effects before run identity is recorded. Detect capabilities without executing a user wrapper outside supervision. Cover failed, cancelled and requested-conversation startup in tests/test_pause.py.

## Expected Behavior

Launchers run only inside supervision and failures retain the intended run identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Regression tests reproduce the original condition and pass reliably after a verified fix, without bypassing identity checks or relying on another account.
close_reason: Merged in PR #59

title: Tauri client screens hub: view revisions and panic isolation
description: Two hardening items from the phase 3a final review (zerus-5wmh.8). (1) Two concurrent pulls of one screen can leave the webview one view behind: latest() keeps the reply of the last request while the hub records the view it computed last, so the next publish finds no change. Put a monotonic revision on each view (screens.rs remember) and let the frontend keep the highest revision (store/latest.ts). (2) The screens ticker is a detached loop and each read runs as a blocking job; a panic in tick or a job would stop polling or leave running/poll.pending set for the session. Wrap tick and each read job in catch_unwind and clear the slot on panic.
notes:
Starting screens hardening while R11 grouping waits for the corrected .47 dependency. Keep the existing view fields and add a monotonic revision; the store applies highest revisions even when request replies complete out of order. Isolate ticker/read-job panics and release the exact affected read slot. No screen design change.

Completion is marked before notifications/dependent reads so a late panic cannot clear a newer slot. Existing account-read bodies remain unchanged. title: mac-install.sh cannot select the Rust toolchain that rust-version requires
description: install.sh runs cargo build --manifest-path from the caller's cwd, and mac-install.sh's remote bash -s only forwards HGS_MOBILE_CONNECTOR. When the Mac's default rustup toolchain is older than Cargo.toml rust-version (Mac default 1.85 with 1.99.1 installed; hgs 1.55.0 needs 1.99), the CLI build fails with 'rustc 1.85.1 is not supported', and a rustup override on ~/.local/src/hgs/.rust-build does not apply. The 0.46.0 rollout needed a temporary override on the Mac home directory. Forward an explicit RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN (or pick the installed toolchain that satisfies rust-version) without changing the machine's default.

title: Mobile Terminal: keep the cursor row in view and follow the bottom
description: Android TerminalScreenView and the iOS TerminalView open the captured pane at the top and keep the scroll offset across snapshots, so on a tall pane the prompt and cursor at the bottom need a manual scroll after opening. MuxPod v0.8.0 (PR #124) follows new output while the view is at the bottom, stops following when the user scrolls away and adds a scroll-to-bottom button with a long-press lock. Adapt this to fixed-size snapshots: bring the native cursor row into view on open, follow it while the user has not scrolled away, and never move during selection.
close_reason: Merged PR #295: mobile Terminal follows the native cursor (bottom/cursor row, right edge on wide panes), pauses on user scroll, Follow cursor resumes, selection never moves. Android emulator smoke + unit tests; iOS ZerusKit tests + simulator build.

title: Mobile Terminal: tappable OSC 8 links with confirmation

title: Run hgs remote shell snippets under sh so fish login shells work
description: hgs @host runs remote commands through the remote login shell. The capability-gated forms in src/cli.rs remote() (wait, session notifications, hooks health, analytics, guide) use POSIX 'if ...; then ...; else ...; fi', and hgs machine ssh uses ${SHELL:-/bin/sh} (src/machines.rs). Both are syntax errors when the remote login shell is fish. MuxPod fixed the same class of bug in v0.8.0 (PR #133, run ephemeral SSH commands under bash). Wrap these snippets in sh -c with exact quoting, keep the plain '~/.local/bin/hgs args' path unchanged, and cover a fish login shell in tests.
close_reason: Merged PR #294 (762465b6): peer POSIX snippets run under sh -c, remote_quote keeps backslashes outside quotes for fish; tests/test_remote_login_shells.py covers sh/bash/zsh/fish, Linux CI installs fish.

title: Self-update installer-based Windows builds from the update feed
description:
Let installer builds update themselves.

Feed:
- The v1 feed rejects unknown artifact kinds, and schema 2 has no Windows kind. Add the Windows installer through a new schema or endpoint that older GUIs never read, and keep v1 unchanged.

Update flow:
1. Download the installer to a private temporary folder with a size bound.
2. Verify the size and SHA-256 against the feed.
3. On signed channels, verify Authenticode with WinVerifyTrust against the expected publisher.
4. Unsigned nightlies are still checked against the feed hash. Orca skips verification entirely for its unsigned dev channel; we keep the hash check.
5. Save drafts, as tray/update-installed.py does.
6. Start the installer silently and exit the GUI. The installer relaunches it.
7. If the update fails, the current installation stays intact.

Channels:
- The installed build identity stays independent of the selected channel.
- Portable builds keep link-only behavior.
- Dev has no Windows build unless it is added explicitly.

Updates never stop agents or the session host. All I/O is bounded and runs in the background.
notes:
2026-10-18, work/windows-installer 2907e886:
- UpdateController reads installation.json to set kind=installer; installer builds stay link-only.
- tray/src/WindowsUpdateTrust: CNG ECDSA P-256 manifest verification plus a WinVerifyTrust publisher check, both covered by test_updates. The trust anchors are empty constants, so selfUpdateConfigured() is false.
Root steering 2026-10-18: no publisher means strictly link-only, never unsigned execution.
Remaining after the owner's key and provider: the signed manifest endpoint, the download and apply flow.

- The staged stable CLI (.local/bin/hgs.exe) is a copy of the signed hgs.exe, so hooks start a signed binary. That reduces Smart App Control and WDAC blocks.

- Unsigned channels stay documented.
- Retries reuse the same candidate.

title: Decide the Windows code signing provider and release approval cadence
description:
Choose who signs Windows binaries, which channels are signed and who approves each release.

SignPath Foundation (free OSS program; signpath.org/terms verified 2026-10-17):
- "Every release needs manual approval for signing."
- A project team member trusted by the team approves, not SignPath staff. SignPath's own review happens once, when the project applies.
- All team members need MFA for both SignPath and GitHub.
- Origin verification requires builds on GitHub-hosted runners.
- The certificate shows "SignPath Foundation" as publisher.
- A "Code signing policy" (roles and privacy policy) must appear on the home and download pages.
- "The project may not contain any proprietary, non open-source component." Ask whether the app-local Microsoft VC++ runtime DLLs in the zip qualify (vcruntime140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll, msvcp140.dll; already Microsoft-signed). If not, decide between a static CRT and the system redistributable. Unsigned upstream OSS DLLs such as Qt are allowed. The Foundation may later require that every included file be signed.

Release cadence:
- 11 stable desktop releases between 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-16 (v0.38.0 to v0.44.0), up to 4 in one day.
- Zip-only means one approval per stable, because SignPath signs PE files inside a zip. An installer means two approvals: inner files first, then the installer.
- Publication waits for the approval.
- Daily nightlies need a daily approval or stay unsigned, as Orca's dev channels do.

Azure Artifact Signing:
- No per-release human approval; it fits nightly automation.
- The publisher is our verified name.
- Needs an eligible organization (USA, Canada, EU, UK) or individual (USA, Canada) and a paid Azure subscription.
- About $9.99 a month for 5,000 signatures.

OV certificate: cloud HSM or token key, renewal at least every 460 days. Its SmartScreen reputation behaves the same as Azure's.

Acceptance: the owner records the provider, the signed channels and the approvers, and the decision is stored with bd remember.
notes:
Owner 2026-10-17 on SignPath: «dll класть можно, нельзя на них подпись менять!» Bundling third-party DLLs (app-local MSVC runtime, Qt, FFmpeg, ConPTY pair) is acceptable; their signatures must never be changed. This settles the MSVC runtime question for the SignPath option.
2026-10-18 decision brief (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-windows-installer-design.md, branch work/windows-installer). The owner chooses:

1. Stable provider:
   - SignPath Foundation: free; publisher 'SignPath Foundation'; one approval per stable, two once the installer exists; MFA for every team member; code signing policy page.
   - Azure Artifact Signing Basic: about $9.99/month. Open to organizations in the US/CA/EU/UK/AU/NZ/JP/KR/SG/CH/NO/IL and to individuals in the US/CA only. The certificate shows the legal name, plus city/state/country for an individual.
   - OV certificate: $150-300/year plus a cloud HSM; shows the legal name.
   - None for now.
2. Nightlies signed or not (recommended: not, under SignPath).
3. Approvers (SignPath).
4. Create the self-update key: an ECDSA P-256 secret in the release environment, created only by the owner.

Recommendation: SignPath for stables unless an eligible legal entity exists; nightlies unsigned. Use the update key for self-update in either case: SignPath's publisher name is shared by every Foundation project, so it cannot identify Zerus.

Not chosen: Certum's OSS card can sign only on the owner's machine, never in CI. The Microsoft Store needs a spike first, because package updates end the package's processes, including the session host. No terms accepted and nothing bought.
Awaiting the owner's choice; see the brief above. Nothing purchased or accepted.

title: Windows distribution: code signing, per-user installer, self-update and winget
description:
Owner direction 2026-10-17: research how other vendors ship Windows desktop apps and record the plan, but do not implement it yet. The portable zip stays the Windows distribution for now.

Current state (verified 2026-10-17): stable releases after 0.42.2 and nightlies carry the unsigned portable zip zerus-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip (v0.44.0 has it). The zip is a GitHub-only asset. The portable GUI defaults to the nightly channel and reads the zerus.dev v1 desktop feed (updates/v1/desktop/<channel>.json, which the mirror builds from GitHub Releases) at most once a day. When a newer product version carries a Windows zip, it links that GitHub release page. There is no installer and no self-update. SmartScreen warns on first start. Smart App Control on Windows 11 blocks unsigned apps with no per-app exemption. AppLocker, WDAC or ASR rules may block the staged hgs.exe that hooks start (see the antivirus and enterprise policy risk in the Windows native host spec).

Research summary (2026-10-17):
- Orca (stablyai/orca, Electron): one per-user NSIS installer, with no zip, MSI or MSIX. Release builds are signed through the SignPath Foundation OSS program in two requests: first the inner PE files including the uninstaller, then the rebuilt installer. Each request needs manual approval; Orca budgets 1 h + 4 h, on GitHub-hosted runners. electron-updater reads GitHub Releases latest.yml + blockmap and checks the Authenticode publisherName. Hourly/daily dev channels ship unsigned with that verification disabled. A release stays a draft until every platform asset exists. A disposable-runner E2E proves the daemon survives an update.
- Zed (Rust): Inno Setup installer signed through Azure Trusted Signing. auto_update_helper.exe swaps files after exit using Restart Manager, with rollback jobs.
- VS Code: Inno Setup user and system installers plus a zip. OBS (Qt): NSIS installer plus its own updater using a manifest and zstd delta patches. Telegram Desktop (Qt): Inno Setup installer plus portable build, with its own updater and signed update packages. Wireshark (Qt): WinSparkle with an Ed25519-signed appcast. KeePassXC (Qt): WiX MSI plus portable zip.
- Signing (Microsoft Learn "Code signing options for Windows app developers", updated 2026-08-29): Azure Artifact Signing costs about $9.99 a month and is open to organizations in the USA, Canada, EU and UK, and to individuals in the USA and Canada only. An OV certificate costs $150-300 a year; its key must sit on an HSM or token since June 2023, and validity is at most 460 days from 2026-03-01. EV certificates lost the instant SmartScreen bypass in 2024. SmartScreen reputation always builds over time.

Constraints for every child:
- Updates never stop agents, session hosts, tmux or resident adapters.
- An installer never touches the content-addressed host images (.local/share/hgs/host), the stable CLI (.local/bin/hgs.exe), or config and state.
- The portable zip stays available.
- Feed compatibility holds: the v1 feed rejects unknown artifact kinds, so new Windows assets stay out of v1.
- Stable publication stays owner-triggered; nightlies stay automatic after full CI.
- Signing credentials live only in a main-only environment and never reach PR code.
- No paid runners.
acceptance_criteria: The owner reactivates the epic; each child closes with its own acceptance. Until then the portable zip remains the Windows distribution.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
Root cause (verified 2026-10-17): on macOS the test never waits for the asynchronous media load. Its guard assumed Darwin's backend, but the bundled official Qt 6.11.2 uses FFmpeg. The play/pause clicks during LoadingMedia make QFFmpegMediaPlayer defer pause(). When the queued load completion (QtConcurrent worker, then invokeMethod) lands in the test's processEvents() after the synthetic positionChanged(5000) and playbackStateChanged(Playing), LoadedMedia applies the pending 7000 ms seek and the deferred pause emits PausedState. That redraws exactly the image captured as `before` (7000 ms, paused), so the check fails.

Failing evidence: main run 39030964535 attempt 1, job 117394569891 (Signed macOS dev candidate / macOS bundle), test_activityview.cpp:1531, both rows use the FFmpeg backend there. Local deterministic reproduction on the Mac against the pinned official Qt (scripts/install-qt-macos.py): holding the global QThreadPool until `before` is captured fails both rows with the same assertion; the player at the check is BufferingMedia, PausedState, position 7000. Homebrew Qt has only the Darwin backend, whose load never completes offscreen, so it cannot show the race.

Fix: check the synchronously updated image before the event-loop turn; document, layout, size, render passes, scroll and selection are still compared after processEvents(). Passing evidence: the same forced late-load ordering passes both rows; 50/50 runs of the test against the pinned official Qt (FFmpeg) and 50/50 against Homebrew Qt 6.11.2 (Darwin); full TestActivityView 192 passed, 1 skipped on both.

The PR only changed src/dsh/bridge.mjs, so the input transport test is intermittent on macOS. Find whether the fixture's NBSP prompt screen is captured before it settles (timing) or the prompt recognizer mis-reads a partial frame, and fix the test wait or the recognizer without weakening the draft-protection assertions.
close_reason: Merged in PR #96: input test screens wait for a unique OSC 2 title with the cursor, not the cursor alone.

title: Claude PostModelSwitch entry stays after a downgrade and blocks older Claude at start
description: Follow-up from zerus-coik (PR #89): once registered, the PostModelSwitch hook entry is never removed, so a Claude older than 2.1.296 later run against the same config dir shows a blocking Settings Warning at every start. hgs already reads the version on every launch while the event is not registered; when it reads a version below the gate and finds the hgs-owned PostModelSwitch entry, remove that entry (only hgs's own hook command, never user entries) before launch.
close_reason: Merged in PR #94: an older Claude gets hgs's PostModelSwitch entry removed before a tracked launch.

title: GUI on macOS: direct QProcess children can inherit ProcessRunner pipe ends
description: Follow-up from zerus-sllg (PR #87): on macOS tray ProcessRunner creates its pipes on a worker thread with pipe() then fcntl(FD_CLOEXEC) (pipeAbove2), while HgsClient starts direct QProcess children on the main thread (machine setup, transfers and others, HgsClient.cpp ~465, 1220, 1345, 1468-1639). Qt forks those without closing inherited fds, so one can inherit a runner child's stdin write end and hold that hgs request open until it exits. Fix with QProcess::setUnixProcessParameters(CloseFileDescriptors) where Qt >= 6.6, or route those children through ProcessRunner, or create runner pipes under a lock shared with QProcess starts.
close_reason: Merged in PR #93: desktop direct QProcess children get only stdio (CloseFileDescriptors on Qt >= 6.8.3).

title: Desktop: a failure callback after an ended launch shows a nameless error
description: Follow-up from the zerus-19do review (PR #82): if a listing reports a launch ended and a failure callback (nativeSessionLaunched with ok=false) arrives afterwards, newSessionLaunchFailed replaces the ended notice; the pending launch is already gone, so the text reads 'Could not start session : <error>'. More likely for non-detached launches (dsh/opencode). Let the ended notice win (or keep the launch name). Also m_endedLaunches never shrinks when no callback follows (terminal launches, restored pending launches): bound or prune it.
close_reason: Merged in PR #84: an ended launch's notice stays over a late failure callback; ended launches are bounded.

title: Audit multi-threaded piped spawns for the macOS pipe inheritance race
description: Follow-up from zerus-jb22 (PR #76): on Apple targets Rust std creates Command pipes with pipe() and sets FD_CLOEXEC afterwards, and posix_spawn does not set CLOEXEC_DEFAULT, so a child spawned by one thread can inherit pipe ends another thread is creating; a child holding another child's stdin open blocks EOF-based protocols. PR #76 serializes spawns in mobile_peers::capture_control only. Audit every place hgs (and the GUI helpers it runs) spawns children with piped stdio from more than one thread at a time (thread::spawn, scoped threads, parallel probes, swarm transports, account probes, speech) and apply a shared spawn lock or fd hygiene where concurrent spawns are possible.
close_reason: Merged in PR #87: concurrent spawners share platform::spawn_in_turn on macOS.

title: Windows host: an ended launch may miss its last screen lines
description: Follow-up from the zerus-ziq3.13 review (PR #67): on the Windows host, launches::screen() captures the supervisor's own pane 100 ms after the agent exits and stops at the first two equal reads. ConPTY output reaches the host asynchronously (the host waits up to 5 s for it to drain before a session ends), so on a slow machine the ended launch's output may lack the last line the agent printed. Use the host's drained output (e.g. launch_status or a host op that returns the final screen after the drain) instead of a fixed settle.
close_reason: Merged in PR #81: the session host completes an ended launch's report from its drained screen; the supervisor's capture stays as fallback.

title: Local ctest runs newsessiondialog on the real desktop
description: 47e4bb2 inserted the newsessiondialog registration between accountusage's zerus_add_test and its offscreen property, so newsessiondialog had no QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. CI exports offscreen globally (scripts/ci/gui.sh), but a local ctest opened real dialogs and focusWhileCatalogLoadsKeepsRememberedAgent failed at qWaitForWindowActive. Make zerus_add_test default every suite to offscreen and restore the misplaced lines.
close_reason: zerus_add_test now defaults every CTest suite to QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen; newsessiondialog and accountusage set it explicitly again. Local ctest without a global platform: 60/60 twice. Commit 6da99b9; CI main #482 (1bfe528, contains it) succeeded.

title: Git status reports a changed remote when the tracking ref lookup fails or times out
description: Follow-up from the zerus-o0po review: in src/state/git_status.rs, a failed or timed-out rev-parse --verify @{upstream} falls back to an empty tracking OID, so remote_check compares the ls-remote hash with an empty string and reports changed (Remote branch changed. Fetch to update). Correct when the tracking ref is genuinely missing locally, misleading when the lookup merely failed; tell the two apart as the upstream lookup now does.
close_reason: Merged in PR #78: only rev-parse --verify --quiet exit 1 with empty stderr counts as a missing tracking ref; other failures keep remote_state unknown.

title: test_discovery_fanout_transports_exit_after_gateway_kill misses a peer transport on macOS
description: PR #69 run 38620207559, macOS CLI job 116045922510 (2026-10-14): tests/test_mobile_peers.py:424 assertTrue(all(path.exists() for path in paths)) failed: not every discovery-pids-<alias> marker appeared within the 10 s window (already widened in 8609b75). The window equals the discovery deadline, so a peer whose identity transport starts late (local identity, then its own support probe, all separate cold processes) is never launched and the test cannot pass. Find which stage is slow on macOS runners and make the test wait for an observable start condition or give the fixture deadline real margin, without weakening the transport-exit assertions.
close_reason: Merged in PR #76: discovery transports spawn under one lock so macOS workers never inherit each other's pipes; the fan-out test waits for the gateway and requires live transports at the kill.

title: Relay answers an oversized declared body with 413 without a bounded drain
description: Follow-up from the zerus-fsup review: when a request declares a body over the cap, the Rust relay returns 413 without the bounded drain that the 429 admission path has, so a client still uploading may see a connection reset instead of the 413. Apply the same bounded drain.
close_reason: Merged in PR #73: the 413 path uses the same bounded discard as the 429 body-capacity refusal.

title: CLI hygiene: Windows usage lists Unix-only commands and session_id accepts a bare dollar sign
description: Follow-ups from the zerus-ziq3.14 review: (1) the Windows usage text still lists hgs clip and hgs notify, which exist only on Unix; (2) session_id() in src/state/rename.rs accepts a bare $ with no digits while attach_command and terminal.rs require at least one digit.
notes: Also: on Windows hgs notify and hgs clip fall through to the launch arm and start an agent instead of refusing; the Windows usage keeps the tmux Ctrl+V clipboard line.
close_reason: Merged in PR #75: Windows refuses notify/clip/paste with exit 2 and drops them and the Ctrl+V line from its usage; rename's session_id requires digits.

title: Recovery may free a Codex account slot on task_started before the provider answers
description: Follow-up from the zerus-a1m2 review: occupies() in src/state/recovery.rs treats provider_status_at after the continuation's user_at as progress. Kimi's TurnStarted was excluded (153e68a). A Codex task_started transcript entry also counts as progress but is not treated as a turn start; if Codex writes it after the prompt-submit hook, the account is freed before the provider answers. Verify Codex ordering against the pinned version and fix if confirmed.
close_reason: Not a bug for the pinned Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0: RegularTask::run awaits emit_turn_started, which persists and flushes the rollout task_started line before the UserPromptSubmit hook runs, so the line can never count as progress after the continuation's user_at. Only repeated rollout write failures at turn setup could reorder it.

title: Git status reports no upstream when the upstream lookup fails or times out
description: Follow-up from the zerus-vnhl review: in src/state/git_status.rs, when the upstream lookup (for-each-ref with local_deadline) fails or times out, text() returns None and inspect() reports remote_state no_upstream, so the GUI says the branch has no upstream. A failed or timed-out lookup should report unknown/unverified instead.
close_reason: Merged in PR #72: a failed or timed-out upstream lookup keeps remote_state unknown instead of no_upstream.

title: hgs read --json shows a Claude approval that the terminal already answered
description: Follow-up from the zerus-h2u review: Claude Terminal approval answers settle from the screen during hgs ls and inspect, but hgs read --json (used by desktop mark-read and the mobile connector) builds its view from the record without reconciling. It can show Needs approval until the next listing or inspect settles it. Reconcile there too, or document why not.
close_reason: Merged in PR #71: hgs read settles Terminal-answered Claude approvals from the screen before comparing marks.

title: Windows: remove remaining tmux wording from user-visible CLI text
description: Follow-up from zerus-ziq3.11 (PR #66, 2026-10-14): the nested-session refusals now name a host session without tmux, but other text a Windows user can reach still says tmux, e.g. 'invalid tmux session identity' in 'hgs a --existing' (src/cli.rs ~1039, src/state/rename.rs) and '... without a tmux Terminal' messages. Make backend-neutral wording on Windows (or everywhere if wording allows) while keeping Unix text byte for byte where tests or users depend on it.
close_reason: Merged in PR #68: Windows CLI text names the session host instead of tmux; Unix text unchanged.

title: Qualify intermittent test_checkout_changes_during_remote_verification_are_not_certified on macOS
description: tests/test_git_status.py GitStatus.test_checkout_changes_during_remote_verification_are_not_certified failed once on the CLI (macos-15) job of PR #59 (run 38607500830, job 116002115554): AssertionError 'ok' != 'changed_during_check'. PR #59 only changes the Codex capability probe in src/state/lifecycle.rs, so the failure looks timing dependent (the checkout change may land before or after the remote verification window on a slow runner). Check how the test injects the checkout change during verification and make the ordering deterministic.
close_reason: Merged in PR #69: the test's git shim no longer intercepts every Git call; it fails only the intended remote verification.

description: Interactive check 2026-10-14. In a local PowerShell session on the Windows host, 'hgs claude MyProj -n x -d' prints 'hgs: already inside tmux session sh/MyProj/work-…; open a new tab'. There is no tmux on Windows; the text should name the session without tmux. Owner: Phase 2.

title: TestNewSessionDialog::refreshKeepsSelectionAndLastReportedLimits counts a late limits probe on macOS
description: PR #52 run 38541058974, macOS desktop job 115775710382: test_newsessiondialog.cpp:234 'probes().size()' was 4, expected 3. The same job passed on main at 5562c2a, so this is intermittent. The test was added or changed by 9fdd148 ('Keep launch limits across token refreshes and refresh them on open'). It records probes().size() after Refresh, fires the 60 s timers and expects no new probe within qWait(100). The refresh now also asks for current limits, so a limits probe that started with the Refresh can land inside that 100 ms. Wait for the Refresh's own limits request to finish (or count only probes started after the timers fire) before taking the baseline, without weakening the no-extra-poll assertion.
close_reason: Already fixed on main by 5e77403 (Wait for opening limit probes before counting later ones); PR #52's run predates it. 0/600 failures under heavy CPU load on current main; 22/60 with the pre-fix test.

title: Audit desktop tests that inject inspections while window polls run
description: zerus-oyjg and zerus-1tu8 (PR #44) shared one hazard: a test injects state with HgsClient::inspectionReady while the window's own inspection or poll is still running, and that reply, read from the fixture before the change, lands afterwards and replaces the injected details. On Windows, Qt 6.10 runs coarse timers of 20 ms or less as multimedia timers that post their QTimerEvent (qeventdispatcher_win.cpp), so a confirmation accepted from a 5 ms QTimer shares a sendPostedEvents() batch with queued ProcessRunner replies, and such a reply can arrive before the dialog's exec() returns. Audit tray/tests (test_sessionswindow.cpp first) for tests that inject inspections with the base fixture program() or a fixture whose inspect reply differs from the injected state, or that act on dialogs from short timers, and apply the zerus-a0ak barrier where needed: setDetailsPollForTests plus waiting for the reply to an inspection the test starts itself. Keep every assertion.
notes: 2026-10-14: nightly 38358653846 (2026-10-13, macOS desktop job 115167602965) failed TestSessionsWindow::clearInspectionUpdatesActivityAndCountersImmediately at test_sessionswindow.cpp:1759 ('timeline.indexOf("Earlier answer")>=0' FALSE), likely the same injected-inspection hazard; that flake alone kept the nightly (and its Windows zip) from publishing that day.
close_reason: Merged in PR #79: keepDetailsPollsOut barrier applied to four exposed tests; the nightly failure itself was fixed by 61e1d21.

title: Qualify intermittent cold-cache compaction test failures on Windows
description: TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheCompactWaitsForSuccess(draft) failed once on the windows-desktop job of PR #42 (run 38514870711, job 115691341904): '!composer->editor()->isReadOnly()' returned FALSE at test_sessionswindow.cpp:2238, after a fixed QTest::qWait(100). It passed in the same PR's previous Windows run and the code path (compaction wait on a remote session) is untouched by M6, so it looks timing dependent on a slow runner. Check whether the editor's read-only state is released by an asynchronous apply/poll and replace the fixed wait with QTRY_VERIFY if so.
notes:
Same family on main without M6: Nightly main (8) run 38513713175 at c9bba3a, job 115687746382: TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation 'shown' returned FALSE at test_sessionswindow.cpp:1774 (windows-desktop). Both look like fixed waits or window-activation timing on the Windows runner.
Related: zerus-oyjg (in progress) qualifies coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation on Windows; coordinate with it rather than fixing the same timing twice.
Recurred on PR #42's next Windows run (run 38516396679, job 115696107822) as coldCacheCompactWaitsForSuccess(cancelled), same line 2238 after QTest::qWait(100). M6 does not touch the compaction or composer paths; 2 of 3 Windows runs of that PR hit this test family, main's CI push runs passed and its nightly hit coldCacheConfirmation (zerus-oyjg).
close_reason: Hardened in PR #44 (be17b70), test only; exact cause not reproduced. The editor's read-only state after the draft outcome comes from MessageComposer::updateControls (waiting, draft loading, sending or the window's session-status block, e.g. 'Refresh the session before sending' after a failed inspection, cleared by the next successful one). The fixed qWait(100) became a QTRY_VERIFY2 on !isReadOnly that names the active lock if it persists; the checks that send.json never appears and the text is unchanged stay strict, so a send that held the lock still fails. Windows test PC: unpatched 96/96 for draft and 48/48 for all rows, 0 hits in 120 CI-like shard runs; fixed 96/96. Not folded into zerus-oyjg: different mechanism. Related audit: zerus-a857.

title: Windows GUI: warn before launching into a session host of another Windows session
description: Spec D5 asks for a warning before the GUI launches into a session host that runs in another Windows session (for example one started over SSH), since its agents then run outside the desktop session. The GUI needs its own session ID (ProcessIdToSessionId) and local_host.windows_session from hgs ls --json. Deferred from M6 (zerus-ziq3.7.11) on 2026-10-14.
notes: PR #46 (2026-10-14): LocalSessionHost rule (Windows-style local machine, running host, windows_session differs from the GUI's ProcessIdToSessionId) and a Launch anyway / Cancel question at every local launch path (New session, resume/restore/resume all/bulk, start fresh, start-to-send, fork, open terminal for a saved session). Linux gui.sh 59/59.
close_reason: Merged in PR #46

title: Windows host: fall back to inbox ConPTY when the bundled OpenConsole cannot load
description: Review finding from the ConPTY pair packaging (M7), 2026-10-14: OpenConsole.exe of Microsoft.Windows.Console.ConPTY 1.25.260930003 statically imports D3DCOMPILER_47.dll. src/host/conpty.rs picks the bundled pair from file presence plus LoadLibrary of conpty.dll, so on a SKU without D3DCOMPILER_47.dll (Server Core) a 'bundled' host would fail session creation instead of falling back to inbox (spec D6: bundled first, inbox as degraded fallback). Make the pair selection also require D3DCOMPILER_47.dll to load from System32 (or detect OpenConsole's start failure) and fall back to inbox, reporting why in session-host status. Desktop Windows 10/11 ship the DLL, so this is insurance, not a Phase 2 blocker.
notes: PR #45 (2026-10-14): the host reads OpenConsole.exe's PE import table (new portable src/host/pe.rs) and uses inbox ConPTY, logging why, when a load-time DLL (API sets aside) is neither next to the server nor in System32. Verified on the Windows PC: host:: 145/145, test_windows_host 7/7. The reason is in the host's start log, not in session-host status.
close_reason: Merged in PR #45: inbox ConPTY when the bundled OpenConsole.exe imports a DLL this Windows lacks

title: Windows: measure hgs start and hook cost under real-time scanning (S7)
description: Spike S7's scanning half: on a Windows machine with real-time scanning on (Defender or a third-party product), measure hgs.exe start (warm and freshly built image), the whole hook path (a Stop through hgs __state hook) and SQLite journal writes against the 5 s hook timeout. The development PC has no real-time scanning: baseline there is about 11 ms warm start, 25 ms start and 37-38 ms whole hook path (S6, 2026-10-14). Split out of M0 (zerus-ziq3.7.1).
notes: 2026-10-14: the development PC's real-time antivirus is Kaspersky (Security Center productState 0x41000, enabled and up to date); only Defender is off. The S6 and S7-baseline numbers (25 ms bare start, 37-38 ms whole hook path p95 <= 41 ms, 132 ms fresh image, 11 ms warm) were therefore measured under Kaspersky real-time protection, far inside the 5 s hook timeout. No Kaspersky exclusion for the test folders is known. Defender's own real-time scanning remains unmeasured. Spec corrected in PR #55.
close_reason: Measured under Kaspersky real-time protection on the development PC (25 ms bare start, 37-38 ms whole hook path, 132 ms fresh image; far inside the 5 s hook timeout); spec corrected in PR #55. Defender's own real-time scanning remains unmeasured.

title: A DeepSeek child cancelled before its first step stays corrupt after disposal
description: Found in the zerus-q55i review (PR #35): a one-shot child cancelled before its first agent/pre-step never records subagent/descriptor and stays in the parent's append-only catalog. While live, the fixed bridge shows an empty page; once stored, every hgs inspect --agent for it fails with 'subagent descriptor is corrupt' (old and new bridge alike). Consider treating a stored child with no own descriptor and no own step/start as never started (empty page) rather than corrupt, keeping real corruption visible.
close_reason: Merged in PR #77: a child with neither descriptor nor step/start is shown as unstarted (empty page) whether live or stored; real corruption stays an error.

title: Codex /clear reset check reads any header above the first prompt row
description: Found in the Windows Phase 2 M4.3 review (2026-10-14), pre-existing on main: clear_context.rs:90 (codex_reset_panel) reads only the rows above the first '›' line, so any Codex screen where the header and folder are still visible above a history prompt or a draft counts as the reset header; only the composer check that follows guards it. Tighten it to the exact post-/clear layout (empty-state panel), with Linux fixtures, as its own change (it alters Linux behaviour).
notes: 2026-10-14: reproduced with real Codex on Linux by the real-agent Windows suite work (zerus-ziq3.7.12): whenever Codex shows the project folder in full in its header (folder outside the home, so not shortened to ~), hgs reports a SessionCleared after the first message and then refuses clear-context. The Linux NativeCodexClear fixture keeps the project under the fixture home, which hides it. Taken by the CI/test-infrastructure session; it blocks gating the windows-host job.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #53 (aa26685). Codex keeps its header above the first history prompt until /clear, so the old reset check (rows above the first '›' row) took a fresh session's answered first message for the reset panel and hgs recorded a false SessionCleared, then refused clear-context. Every new session of real Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0 did this; the resumed native fixture hid it. The reset now needs exactly one '›' row, the composer, empty or with one of the two reviewed placeholders, with only the header block above it. Real captures from both pins, Phase 2's 110x35 fixtures and Windows forms in unit tests; a native NativeCodexClear regression (folder outside the fixture home) fails on the old binary for both pins and passes now; full Linux Codex matrix green (12 tests x 4 configs x 2 pins, including rpcv's async question cases); Windows real-agent suite green on the test PC.

title: Codex Update now reports delivery uncertain when the installer runs over 2 s
description: Found while fixing zerus-y0a8 (PR #27): real Codex leaves raw mode before installing an update, so after Update now the terminal check cannot pass while the installer runs. kimi_tui_choice now waits for the pinned process to exit within the existing 2 s acknowledgement deadline; an installer that runs longer is still reported as 'delivery uncertain' (no key is resent). Decide whether Update now should accept a longer, explicitly bounded installer phase (for example by recognizing the installer output or the agent's exit) instead of the uncertain result; the native Codex suite currently answers only skip choices.
close_reason: Merged in PR #88: Codex Update now is confirmed by its installer announcement within a bounded 15 s phase.

title: Run pinned Claude Code native suites on macOS CI
description: Linux CI now runs all Claude native suites against the pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64 package (zerus-m6ph). macOS still needs a manual HGS_CLAUDE_TEST_BIN. Pin the official darwin-arm64 package per version with SHA-512, make scripts/ci/agent-compatibility.py select the host platform's pin, verify all 44 tests on macos-15 before enabling the step there, and keep Codex Linux-only unless separately reviewed.
close_reason: 213013c pins darwin-arm64 Claude Code 2.1.296 and runs the Claude matrix on macOS CI; it also fixed wrapped workspace paths in Claude trust recognition and gave native answers a 60 s test budget. 5aedef6 renews the Other-clearing window on verified progress after macOS CI hit the fixed 5 s limit. CI run 38455524232: macOS 51/51 and Linux Claude/Codex matrices passed, 0 skipped, whole run green.

title: Record Claude PostModelSwitch for exact model confirmation
description: Claude Code 2.1.296 fires PostModelSwitch with from_model, to_model (exact ID), requested_model and source (command, picker, sdk, auto, resume). hgs does not register it, so a /model change made in Terminal is seen only through the transcript receipt (display name) or the next turn. Registering it would give the exact model immediately, including Terminal and automatic switches. Verify that older reviewed Claude versions accept an unknown hook event in settings before adding it to src/state/hooks.rs, and keep PreModelSwitch unregistered: its allow would skip Claude's cache-miss confirmation for the user too.
close_reason: Merged in PR #89: PostModelSwitch records the exact model for Claude >= 2.1.296.

title: Make subprocessTimeoutLeavesEventLoopResponsive detect a blocked event loop
description: Found in the zerus-fbjy.6 review (2026-10-13). tray/tests/test_updates.cpp subprocessTimeoutLeavesEventLoopResponsive checks a 30 ms single-shot tick with QTRY_VERIFY_WITH_TIMEOUT(tick,1000). Qt 6 QTRY evaluates the expression once more after its loop, so the tick turns true as soon as a blocked loop resumes; neither the old 5 s nor the new 1.5 s package-manager deadline lets the check detect a synchronous probe. Measure the tick's delay with a QElapsedTimer instead, so a blocking probe fails the test.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #18 (merged 0ecd348): subprocessTimeoutLeavesEventLoopResponsive measures the longest pause between 20 ms ticks from before the controller exists and fails above 1 s against the 1.5 s deadline; canonicalOwnershipAsync holds the pacman owner query until the test has seen it start. Both fail with a synchronous probe, also from the constructor (reviewed with mutations).

title: Unlock CLI file locks explicitly instead of relying on handle close
description: On Windows, LockFileEx locks on a closed handle are released by the OS later, at a time that 'depends upon available system resources' (Microsoft LockFileEx docs), so a short-lived hgs process that only drops its lock file can make the next process see contention. state/storage.rs Guard, worktrees.rs and worktree_cleanup.rs already unlock explicitly; metrics.rs was fixed after a Windows CI flake (briefly_held_lock_delays_sampling_instead_of_failing). Remaining sites that only drop the handle: config.rs, machines.rs, accounts.rs (try_lock), accounts/mcp_servers.rs, accounts/claude_settings.rs, mobile_peers.rs (bounded try_lock), swarm/store.rs, swarm/transport.rs (bounded try_lock), state/recovery.rs. Bounded try_lock waits are the ones that can fail. Prefer one shared guard that calls fs2::FileExt::unlock in Drop (UFCS, so Rust 1.89+ std File::unlock is not picked).
close_reason: All fs2 lock sites in src/ now hold platform::FileLock, which unlocks explicitly on drop (state::storage::Guard is an alias). Successful shared worker probes release at once. Regression test: dropping the guard releases the lock while a duplicate handle stays open. Verified locally and on Windows (cargo test, clippy 1.85 -D warnings, Windows client tests).

title: Cached .lnk attachments are judged by their shortcut target on Windows
description: Qt on Windows treats any existing path ending in .lnk as a shortcut: QFileInfo isFile(), size() and canonicalFilePath() describe the shortcut's target. AttachmentFiles::cachedAt() therefore reports a correctly cached .lnk attachment as unavailable when its target is a folder, missing, offline, empty or larger than the attachment limit, so Retry and readAsync fail with 'The saved attachment is unavailable or changed'. storeAt() no longer writes through shortcuts (fixed with the concurrent-store change). Possible fix: never let a cached name end in .lnk (for example append '_'), or size-check the opened handle instead of QFileInfo for such names, and add a cached()/readAsync assertion to cachedShortcutNeverWritesThroughToItsTarget.
close_reason: Cached attachment names never end in .lnk, a dot or a space, avoid Windows device names, and fit 240 bytes and 180 units while keeping the extension. Downloads, file drops, staging and the composer judge a Windows .lnk as the file QFile reads (tray/src/LocalFile.h). New tests fail on the old sources on Windows and pass on the new ones.

title: macOS recovery LaunchAgent respawns every 10 s while a detached worker holds the lock
description: Observed 2026-10-12 on a Mac: com.hgdev.hgs-recovery showed no PID and 'spawn scheduled' with over 1,800 runs, each exiting 0, while an 'hgs recovery worker' started by ensure_worker() (setsid, parent launchd) held recovery/worker.lock. worker() returns 0 when the lock is taken, and KeepAlive=true with ThrottleInterval=10 relaunches it indefinitely. Recovery itself works, but the managed job never owns the worker and wastes a process spawn every 10 s. The race appears after a service restart (kickstart -k) when any hgs invocation spawns a detached worker first. Consider waiting for the lock in the managed worker, having a detached worker yield to the service, or KeepAlive on unsuccessful exit only. Check whether Linux systemd (Restart policy) can loop the same way.
close_reason: Merged in PR #110: the recovery service's worker waits holding a service lock instead of exiting; detached workers yield. Confirm on a Mac after the next install.

title: macOS swarm installer can unload the worker when its plist changes during a restart

The install aborted after the CLI step and the swarm LaunchAgent stayed unloaded until a rerun bootstrapped it. Wait for bootout to complete (or bootstrap after a changed plist) instead of kickstarting a service being removed.
notes: Fixed: scripts/launchd_agent.py waits (bounded, 15 s) for launchctl print to fail after bootout of a changed definition, then bootstraps; kickstart runs only for an unchanged loaded agent and reports failures. Swarm and recovery installers share it; caller PATH is split so duplicate directories collapse. tests/test_launchd_agent.py fakes the asynchronous removal observed on macOS.
close_reason: Fixed in ad263e8. Verified on the Mac: mac-install.sh reloaded the changed swarm and recovery definitions through bootout, wait and bootstrap without a kickstart race; both workers run and native processes were unchanged.

title: macOS swarm worker survives install-time kickstart -k
description: 2026-10-11 on the owner's Mac: after ./install.sh replaced ~/.local/bin/hgs (01:29), com.hgdev.hgs-swarm still ran PID 14560 started 2026-10-10 14:01 (launchctl print: runs = 2, last terminating signal = Terminated: 15), while the recovery worker restarted. scripts/install-swarm-service.py runs launchctl kickstart -k with check=True and install succeeded, so the worker likely ignores or outlives the restart and keeps running an older binary. Determine whether this is intended and make updates take effect.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
2026-10-18 root cause and source fix (lane branch mac/lifecycle-lane, commit 9aa08d2b on base dfe25722; not integrated).

Live state on the owner Mac (read-only, nothing changed):
- com.hgdev.hgs-swarm (runs 50654+) and com.hgdev.hgs-recovery (runs 53515+) are in "spawn scheduled" with job state "spawn failed" and last exit code 78 (EX_CONFIG). Their properties include "needs LWCR update | managed LWCR | has LWCR".
- launchd logs every 10 s: "Service could not initialize: Unable to get updated LWCR for (<UUID>, <plist>, 501), error 0x3 - No such process". backgroundtaskmanagementd logs getItemWithUUID for that UUID.
- swarm.log was last written 2026-10-12 18:37, by the exit-on-replacement line; the workers have been down since then.
- The voice agent (same hgs, reloaded 2026-10-12 18:37:41, no LWCR properties) and the session bridge (plist from 2026-10-07) respawn fine after binary updates.
- So the cause is a launch constraint from the Login Items record, attached to these two loaded agents and naming an earlier ad-hoc build. A binary update alone does not cause it. The trigger is unverified: testing it needs a plist in the real LaunchAgents folder, which was not done.
- Remedy (owner/root decision, not applied): bootout plus bootstrap of each label.

Isolated launchd evidence (fixture labels org.example.zerus-zu0s-*, scratch plists, private HOME):
- Current worker 1.54.0: after its executable is replaced, including by a valid ad-hoc build with another code hash, it exits within one round (exit 1). launchd starts the new image (runs 2), and kickstart -k and bootout/bootstrap both restart it.
- Pre-fix worker 1.46.1 (21683e1f): it keeps running after replacement until install(restart=True) kickstarts it (runs 2, SIGTERM). This is the original report.
- Narrow startup race (not fixed): Executable::current() on macOS reads the path, not the running image. A replacement within about 0.1 s of start, or a missing path at start, disables detection. Recovery uses path mtime the same way.

Fix:
- scripts/launchd_agent.install reloads (bootout, wait, bootstrap) instead of kickstart when restarting, and also reloads a loaded agent that has no pid and last failed to start (job state "spawn failed" or exit 78). install.sh and zerus-setup --workers therefore repair it.
- The installation guide drops the stale "workers keep the previous binary until kickstarted" text and documents the reload.

Tests:
- tests.test_launchd_agent: 7 pass. Against the original launchd_agent, 4 fail or error.
- test_launchd_agent + test_macos_setup + test_mac_install + test_mobile_connector_service: 57 OK, 14 systemd skips.
- Real launchd: a fixture whose program is missing is detected as stalled from real launchctl print output, an unchanged no-restart install reloads it into a running pid, a healthy agent is left unchanged, and restart reloads it to a new pid.
- check-source and privacy: clean.

title: Avoid fork() malloc-lock stalls when launching hgs on macOS
description: After zerus-ilix.5, hgs children start on the ProcessRunner worker thread, but on macOS Qt's vforkfd falls back to fork(), whose atfork handlers (_malloc_fork_prepare/_malloc_fork_parent) hold every malloc zone lock for the duration of the fork (~4 ms in the large GUI process per the 2026-10-10 profile). A GUI-thread allocation during that window still waits. Options: posix_spawn-based launching on macOS inside ProcessRunner, or fewer launches through a long-lived hgs stream for local polls.
acceptance_criteria: A profile of the live macOS app shows no GUI-thread waits on malloc locks caused by hgs launches; Linux behavior is unchanged or improved; process I/O, timeouts, environment and cancellation semantics stay identical.
notes: 2026-10-10 experiments (macOS 27, M1 Pro, 40k-region process): fork 12.5-15 ms vs posix_spawn 0.27-0.30 ms per launch, but concurrent malloc (mixed sizes) and mmap+page-fault+munmap in another thread showed no stalls with either (worst <1 ms both). GUI-thread waits from worker forks are not reproducible; the remaining benefit is fork CPU (~4 ms per launch in the live GUI, ~0.4% of a core). Owner decision: implement the macOS posix_spawn backend anyway, alongside reducing hgs ls poll cost.
close_reason: macOS ProcessRunner starts children with posix_spawn (6140fdb): ~7.5 ms -> ~0.2 ms CPU per launch in a large process; live GUI worker 30 s: fork 116 ms -> posix_spawn 17 ms. GUI-thread stalls from worker forks were not reproducible. Full suites passed on macOS and Linux; installed on the Mac.

title: Stabilize account-loading test under parallel GUI test load
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run GUI tests with ctest --test-dir tray/build -j 4.

The account-loading test reliably verifies incremental local-first loading under parallel test load and continues to detect real grouping regressions.

title: A rename that commits during a listing can show the session twice

If live() runs after rename's tmux rename-session but records() runs before rename commits the binding move, one listing can show a stateless live row under the new name plus the old-name binding as stopped. Read the records under the state lock (or re-read them after the panes and reconcile by session id) so a rename is seen atomically, without blocking listings on long renames.

title: A session renamed between tmux list-sessions and list-panes drops out of one listing

If a session is renamed between list-sessions and list-panes, the old name has no panes and is dropped, and the saved record is skipped because the new name is live, so the session is missing from that one listing (before PR #97 it showed under its old name as a stateless row with its launch_id). Plausible, not reproduced; decide whether to look up the record by session id/launch id instead of name.

title: DeepSeek bridge: settings and send accept a child id and install or change its selection

title: DeepSeek: read-only list and inspect install model selection listeners on children

A read thus mutates the child (adds prompt-assembly listeners). Decide whether reads should ever install them; if not, read the selection without installing (projection or a non-installing accessor) and keep live selection changes working.
close_reason: Merged in PR #83: read-only list/inspect read selections without installing them on children.

title: Desktop: a late launch success callback can replace an ended-launch notice

Loading activity…' and sets m_nativeLaunchToOpen to an ID that never appears (tray/src/SessionsWindow.cpp). The window is the few milliseconds between started() and process exit plus SSH teardown. Make an ended launch win over a later success callback for the same launch ID.
close_reason: Merged in PR #82: an ended launch's notice stays over a late success callback.

title: Relay: discard bodies on refusals made before body reading

title: Measure Qt tests per function and shard by row
description: Deferred from the CI speed-up plan: per-function JUnit, row-level sharding of sessionswindow, Windows fake-CLI fast path, worker-count experiments.
notes:
2026-10-13 va-kids (Windows 11, Python 3.13.12): one fake-CLI call through the test helper shim costs 56 ms median (helper alone 7 ms; python -I -X utf8 -B with a json/pathlib fixture 39 ms; adding -S saves only 2 ms). A SessionsWindow fixture issues about 9 such calls at start-up (recovery get, project ls, account inspect, swarm initialize, inspect). Decide on a Windows fast path only from per-function CI timings (hosted runners are several times slower than va-kids).
Measured 2026-10-13. PR #16 run 38388803214 (balanced shards): Windows sessionswindow shards 36-75 s (sum 560 s), Qt step 204 s (was 214 s); the step is bound by total work at -j4, not by the longest shard. Linux strace of the whole suite: about 3060 fixture calls (inspect 706, project ls 592, recovery get 579, account inspect 445, swarm initialize 269). va-kids per call: helper 7 ms, python -c pass 23 ms, json import about 10 ms more (re/enum), pathlib about 14 ms, runpy about 5 ms; whole shim call 56 ms. A pycache_prefix gives nothing (stdlib already precompiled); exec instead of runpy saves only 5 ms. Only a worker that reuses one interpreter across calls removes most of the cost: estimated 140-150 s CPU, about 35-40 s off the Windows Qt step.
Implemented 2026-10-13 in PR #16 (commit 'Run Windows Qt fixtures in a warm Python worker pool'): each Windows test program names a pool (ZERUS_FIXTURE_POOL, set by TestIsolation.cpp; 0 disables it) and the shim hands calls outside a console to at most six warm workers (tray/tests/support/fixture-worker.py) over a named pipe; the worker exits when its shim dies or its test program ends. va-kids -j4: Qt suites 141 s -> 114 s, all pass, no leftover workers. Hosted CI run 38393612390: Windows Qt step 204 s -> 167 s; whole PR run 7m57s -> 7m25s.
close_reason: Done in PR #16 and #17: per-function QtTest JUnit in artifacts/test-results/qt-functions; duration-balanced shards with an exactly-once check, seed from CI via scripts/ci/qt-shard-seed.py; ZERUS_PYTHON_JOBS 8/6; Windows warm Python fixture pool (Qt step 204 s -> 124 s on main with the other changes); settings reset per test and atomic fixture data writes for shard-order independence; ccache bypass for localized MSVC.
